If the chain breaks at an unknown ancestor before reaching a library, the value is a lower bound and the message says at least; it is only reported when that bound already exceeds the limit. Units of a library itself are not checked. The finding sits on the class name; the metrics lens shows the depth next to the member count.
rules.bad: TBasis = class(TForm) ... TStufe6 = class(TStufe5)  { 6 own ancestors }
rules.good:
TStufe2 = class(TBasis)
  FDruck: IDruck;  { composition instead of more levels }

options.name: max
options.description: Highest allowed number of own ancestors.

rules.name: Public field
rules.description: Fields in the public or published section of a class. The section without a visibility keyword only counts for classes without an ancestor or with TObject, because the form designer puts its fields there. Records are excluded unless includeRecords is set; class var is not reported. Off by default. Quick fix: Encapsulate field moves the field as FName into a private section at the end of the class and adds property Name read FName write FName in the old section; accesses from outside stay valid.

options.name: includeRecords
options.description: Also report fields of records.

rules.name: Non-generic list with cast
rules.description: A non-generic TList (System.Classes) or TObjectList (System.Contnrs) whose items are read with a cast: T(List[I]), T(List.Items[I]), T(List.First), List[I] as T and so on. TList<T> and TObjectList<T> from System.Generics.Collections check the type at compile time and need no cast. The rule reports once per list, at its declaration when it is in this file, otherwise at the first cast; with several target types, all of them are named. Only when name resolution finds the list type and the target type for sure; casts to Pointer are ignored. Off by default; for code that must still compile with old Delphi versions, use exclude. Quick fix (#1105): converts the list to TList<T> or TObjectList<T> in one step: declaration, every Create (arguments are kept), every cast and System.Generics.Collections in the uses clause; Contnrs is removed when nothing else uses it. Only when every read has the same cast and no member without a generic counterpart is used (Sort with TListSortCompare, Assign with TListAssignOp, List), no Pointer or Integer values are stored, Add, Extract, Remove and IndexOf get T, and the list is not passed on. If the list is visible outside the unit, the fix also rewrites the other units of the project group or is not offered; "fix all" (source.fixAll) never applies such fixes. Otherwise the finding hover names the reason. Stacks and queues: legacy-stack-queue.

rules.name: Non-generic stack or queue with cast
rules.description: A non-generic TStack, TQueue, TObjectStack or TObjectQueue (System.Contnrs) whose items are read with a cast: T(Stack.Pop), T(Stack.Peek), Queue.Pop as T and so on. TStack<T>, TQueue<T>, TObjectStack<T> and TObjectQueue<T> from System.Generics.Collections check the type at compile time and need no cast. Like legacy-tlist, the rule reports once per stack or queue, at its declaration when it is in this file, otherwise at the first cast; with several target types, all of them are named. Only when name resolution finds the type and the target type for sure; casts to Pointer are ignored. Off by default; for code that must still compile with old Delphi versions, use exclude. Quick fix: converts in one step like legacy-tlist; for queues Push becomes Enqueue and Pop becomes Dequeue. TObjectStack<T> and TObjectQueue<T> own their objects, the Contnrs classes do not: the fix therefore creates them with Create(False) and reads with Extract, because Pop and Dequeue are procedures there that free the object. Without a Create in the unit, with different casts or with members without a generic counterpart (AtLeast) there is no fix; the finding hover names the reason.

rules.name: Global variable in interface
rules.description: var or threadvar in the interface section of a unit: every unit that uses it can read and change the value. The form variable created by the designer (frmMain: TfrmMain, for classes derived from TForm, TFrame, TDataModule or any class in a unit with a form file) is excluded unless includeFormVariables is set. Off by default. Move the variable into the implementation section and offer a function or property instead.

options.name: includeFormVariables
options.description: Also report the form variables created by the designer.

rules.name: Commented-out code
rules.description: At least minLines consecutive comment lines (// per line or a multi-line { } comment) that parse as statements, declarations or class members. Prose at the start and end of the block is ignored, and at least half the lines must look like code (;, :=, begin, end, then, do). XMLDoc (///) and comments before the first token (license headers) are never reported. Confidence medium. Version control keeps the old code; the fix removes the lines.
rules.good: Speichern;

options.name: minLines
options.description: Minimum number of consecutive commented-out code lines.

rules.name: Default parameter instead of overload
rules.description: A parameter with a default value (Count: Integer = 10). For teams that prefer overloads: default values end up compiled into the caller, do not change with the library and do not mix well with overloads. Reported once per declaration (class member, interface section, forward or a routine only in the implementation part); the body of a declaration is not reported again. The quick fix inserts one overload per omitted trailing default parameter before the declaration, each forwarding with the default value, removes the default values (also repeated ones in the body) and adds overload. No fix when the signature is given from outside (virtual, dynamic, abstract, override, message, external, interface types), when the name is used as a value (@Routine, method pointer), when an overload of the same name exists, inside conditional compilation, or when the body cannot be found unambiguously.
rules.bad: procedure Exportieren(const Datei: string; MitKopf: Boolean = True);
rules.good:
procedure Exportieren(const Datei: string); overload;
procedure Exportieren(const Datei: string; MitKopf: Boolean); overload;

rules.name: Empty routine
rules.description: A method or routine whose body has neither a statement nor a comment (nor a compiler directive). Either the content is missing or the method can go. Not reported: virtual and dynamic methods (a stand-in for abstract in base classes), message handlers, methods of classes that list interfaces (the compiler requires every interface method), event handlers named in the form file (the IDE removes empty ones when saving) and bodies with a comment, such as overrides that deliberately do nothing. Quick fixes: insert a comment between begin and end; remove the method (declaration with its XML doc and body) only for private methods and routines without a declaration in the interface part that occur nowhere else in the file and fulfil no signature from outside.

rules.name: Accessor method only reads or writes a field
rules.description: A getter whose body is only Result := FName; (also Exit(FName), Self.FName) or a setter whose body is only FName := Value; (with refactoring.inlineAccessorEqualityCheck also if FName <> Value then FName := Value;). The property can point to the field directly. Only methods that are not virtual, dynamic, override or abstract, not class methods, not overloaded or generic, implement no interface method (also via a method resolution clause), have no index specifier and are not used by other members of the class; the field belongs to the class and has the type of the property. Silent unless refactoring.inlineAccessorDiagnostic is on (default off) and refactoring.inlineAccessor is on. Medium confidence: calls in other units are not visible to the rule. No quick fix in the rule; the code action "Replace accessor GetName with field FName" at the same place checks calls with the reference search and replaces it.
rules.good: property Name: string read FName write FName;

rules.name: Property without read
rules.description: A property has write but no read. It cannot be shown in the Object Inspector or read in the debugger and confuses callers. Properties without a type are skipped (they republish an inherited property whose read comes from the ancestor), as are properties with an attribute from allowAttributes (with or without the Attribute suffix). Quick fix: add read FName when the type declares a field FName of the same type. Reading such a property is reported by readonly-property-assigned.
rules.bad: property Passwort: string write SetPasswort;
rules.good: property Passwort: string read FPasswort write SetPasswort;

options.name: allowAttributes
options.description: Attributes that allow a property without read.

rules.name: XMLDoc does not match the signature
rules.description: A /// comment does not match its declaration or is not well-formed XML, like the compiler warnings W1201 to W1208 with XML documentation enabled. Reported: <param> for a parameter that does not exist; missing <param> when the block describes parameters at all (like W1208, 'but other parameters do'); with checkReturns, <returns> on a routine without a result and missing <returns> on a function whose block describes parameters. <inheritdoc/> fills in what is missing. Also '<' and '&' outside tags and entities, unknown entities, attribute values without quotes, unclosed and stray end tags, and cref targets that do not exist (W1206, only with an index and when every unit in uses is known; generic targets, unit names and types with unknown ancestors stay silent). With requirePublic, public and published methods and properties of types in the interface section without a /// comment are reported too (not override, not properties without a type). Quick fixes: rename unknown <param> in order to the missing ones, add the rest as empty lines in signature order, remove surplus <param> and stray <returns>; escape the character, add quotes, add or remove the end tag, write an unknown empty tag like TList<T> as text; set cref to the most similar symbol; generate the comment skeleton.

options.name: requirePublic
options.description: Also report public members without XMLDoc.

options.name: checkReturns
options.description: Check <returns>.

rules.name: TThread.Queue(nil, …) in a package
rules.description: TThread.Queue(nil, …) or TThread.ForceQueue(nil, …) in a unit of a design-time or runtime package: the entry belongs to no thread, so nobody removes it when the package is unloaded, and CheckSynchronize may call it afterwards in memory that no longer holds the code. Package units are recognized through the .dpk or .dproj of the loaded project (a .dpk on its own without project). A line with the comment from okMarker (default mainthread-ok) is exempt. High confidence. Quick fix: rewrite to the wrapper from the wrapper option (default TAtlasMainThread.Queue, ForceQueue for ForceQueue); with a parenthesis the wrapper text is put in front of the remaining arguments. ForceQueue with a delay gets no quick fix. The command-line linter reads the .dpk files below the checked folder. Does the same as Tools/Check-MainThreadQueue.ps1 for any plugin project; the script stays for checks without the Atlas server.

options.name: wrapper
options.description: Replacement for TThread.Queue(nil, in the quick fix.

options.name: okMarker
options.description: Comment that exempts a line.

rules.name: IDE notifier without RemoveNotifier
rules.description: AddNotifier on IOTAServices, IOTAEditorServices, IOTAModule and so on (or another pair from registerPairs) whose index never reaches RemoveNotifier: the call is a statement without assignment, or the variable it is assigned to is never passed to RemoveNotifier in the unit (in finalization, a destructor or Destroyed). The IDE then calls the notifier after the package is unloaded, in memory that no longer holds the code. Register… calls inside the procedure Register are exempt: the IDE removes those wizards itself. Medium confidence. Quick fix in methods: keep the index in a field (FNotifierIndex in the private section) and add RemoveNotifier to the destructor, which is created if missing; in procedures of the unit: a global variable initialized with -1 and RemoveNotifier in finalization. No quick fix when the receiver is a parameter or local variable.

options.name: registerPairs
options.description: Pairs of the Open Tools API as [{"open": "AddNotifier", "close": "RemoveNotifier"}]; replaces the default.

rules.name: DUnitX test without assert
rules.description: A [Test] or [TestCase] method that calls no check, neither itself nor through methods of the same class or routines of the unit: it is always green. Calls matching assertPatterns (default Assert.*, WillRaise*, Check*), System.Assert and calls on classes with Assert in their name (TRuleAssert.Reports) count as checks. Tests with [WillRaise] or [Ignore] stay silent. High confidence. Quick fixes: insert Assert.Pass as a placeholder, or jump to the method.

options.name: assertPatterns
options.description: Calls that count as a check, as patterns with * and ?; replaces the default.

rules.name: Event called without Assigned check
rules.description: FOnChange(Self) or OnChange(Self) is called in a method of the class without Assigned(FOnChange) or FOnChange <> nil guarding the call: without a handler an access violation follows. Events are fields and properties of the class with a method pointer or reference type (procedure ... of object, reference to ..., TNotifyEvent, TProc/TFunc, types ending in Event, procedural types of the unit or the index). Guards: the then branch of a condition with Assigned (also while), the else branch of not Assigned, "Assigned(F) and" before the call, or "if not Assigned(F) then Exit/raise" before it, including a flag variable or a parameterless method of the class whose Result contains Assigned(F). Fields that a constructor sets to a value (injected dependencies such as FReadText := AReadText), properties reading them and local names that shadow the event stay silent. High confidence. Quick fix: wrap the call in "if Assigned(F) then" when it is a statement of its own in a block.

rules.name: Item of an owning list freed as well
rules.description: An item of a TObjectList/TObjectList<T> (OwnsObjects, default True) or of a TObjectDictionary with doOwnsValues is freed with Free, FreeAndNil, Destroy or DisposeOf, directly (List[I].Free, List.Items[I].Free) or through a variable taken from List[I], List.First/Last or a for-in loop over the list or Dictionary.Values. The list frees the item itself on Delete, Remove, Clear, an assignment to List[I], or at the latest when it is freed: a double free. A list is owning when the unit creates it that way (TObjectList without False, TObjectDictionary with doOwnsValues) or declares it as TObjectList without creating it, and no OwnsObjects := False follows. Extract in the same routine keeps the rule silent. High confidence. Quick fixes: remove the Free (the whole loop when it only frees), Delete or Remove instead of Free, Extract instead of Remove.

rules.name: Object created and lost at once
rules.description: TStringList.Create; as a statement of its own: the object is created but stored nowhere and never freed (memory leak). Silent for components with an owner (first argument Self, Owner, AOwner, Application, or a TComponent descendant with an argument other than nil), threads (they free themselves with FreeOnTerminate), records, unknown classes with arguments and classes listed in selfRegistering. High confidence. Quick fix: assign to a new local variable and wrap the following statements of the block in try/finally with Free.

options.name: selfRegistering
options.description: Classes that register themselves in their constructor, as patterns with * and ?; Create as a statement stays silent for them.

rules.name: GetMem or New without release
rules.description: A local variable receives memory from GetMem, AllocMem, ReallocMem, GetMemory, New, StrAlloc or StrNew, but the routine never releases it with FreeMem, FreeMemory, Dispose, StrDispose or ReallocMem(P, 0), and the pointer neither leaves the routine nor is stored: not returned (Result, Exit), not assigned to another variable or field, not passed by address (@P), not handed to a method that keeps it (Add, Insert, Push …), not captured by an anonymous method and not used in a local routine. Passing the pointer to read or fill it (Checksum(P, N), Stream.ReadBuffer(P^, N)) is fine; a routine whose name contains Free, Frei, Release, Dispose, Destroy or Dealloc counts as the release. A release without try/finally is reported by pair-without-finally. Medium confidence. Quick fix: wrap the following statements of the block in try … finally with the matching release.

rules.name: Objects in a TStringList without ownership
rules.description: AddObject or InsertObject puts a newly created object (T.Create(…) directly, or a local variable created that way and otherwise only read) into a TStringList (or THashedStringList) that the unit creates without OwnsObjects, or into the Items of a TListBox, TComboBox, TCheckListBox, TComboBoxEx or TColorListBox field; nobody frees these objects. A list is owning with TStringList.Create(True) or OwnsObjects := True. Silent when a routine of the unit reads List.Objects[…] and frees something, when the list is passed on (FreeObjects(List), assigned elsewhere), when the object has an owner (Self, Owner, AOwner, Application or a TComponent descendant with an argument) and for lists not created in the unit. Medium confidence. Quick fix: TStringList.Create(True) (also instead of Create(False)), with other constructors OwnsObjects := True after the creation; none for control items.

rules.name: Message handler without inherited
rules.description: A method with message WM_... or CM_... calls neither inherited nor DefaultHandler (or DefWindowProc, CallWindowProc). The default handling of the VCL or Windows is lost: no realignment on WM_SIZE, no closing on WM_CLOSE, no painting on WM_PAINT. The message names the consequence for common messages. Silent for classes without an ancestor, for messages listed in swallow (default WM_ERASEBKGND) and for handlers that set Msg.Result themselves (deliberate answer such as MA_NOACTIVATE). Medium confidence. Quick fix: insert inherited; at the start.

options.name: swallow
options.description: Messages that may be handled without inherited; replaces the default.

rules.name: String index from 0 or Pos result compared with -1
rules.description: The classic string routines count from 1: Copy(S, 0, N) and Insert(T, S, 0) only work like 1 by chance, Delete(S, 0, N) deletes nothing. The string must be known: declared type in the file, literal, or .Text/.Caption; dynamic arrays (0-based) stay silent. Pos, PosEx and AnsiPos return 0 for no match: Pos(...) > -1, >= 0 and <> -1 are always true, = -1 and < 0 never. Conversely S.IndexOf(...) > 0 or >= 1 misses a match at the start, < 1 or <= 0 counts it as not found (medium confidence; LastIndexOf stays silent, where > 0 usually means "not at the start"). High confidence for Delete and Pos. Quick fix: start value 1 or the corrected comparison (> 0, = 0, >= 0, < 0).
rules.bad:
if Pos(';', Zeile) > -1 then
  Felder := Copy(Zeile, 0, Pos(';', Zeile) - 1);
rules.good:
if Pos(';', Zeile) > 0 then
  Felder := Copy(Zeile, 1, Pos(';', Zeile) - 1);

rules.name: DelimitedText without StrictDelimiter
rules.description: List.DelimitedText := ... after List.Delimiter := ... in the same routine without StrictDelimiter being set: DelimitedText then also splits at spaces, 'Max Muster;Berlin' becomes three entries instead of two. For fields, StrictDelimiter anywhere in the unit counts (often in the constructor); StrictDelimiter := False is deliberate and stays silent, as does DelimitedText without a Delimiter of its own. High confidence. Quick fix: insert StrictDelimiter := True; before the assignment.
rules.bad:
Teile.Delimiter := ';';
Teile.DelimitedText := Zeile;

rules.name: Self passed as interface during construction
rules.description: Self is passed as an interface while reference counting can already free the object. Only two real error cases are reported: (1) a class with its own reference counting (an _Release in the class chain frees the object, no class overrides NewInstance, the chain is known up to TObject) passes Self as an interface in a constructor or in AfterConstruction: the counter goes from 0 to 1 and back to 0, the object is destroyed before construction ends. (2) A TInterfacedObject descendant passes Self as an interface in AfterConstruction after inherited: inherited AfterConstruction has already removed the protective count from NewInstance. In the constructor of a TInterfacedObject descendant Self is protected and the rule stays silent. Passing counts as Self as IX, IX(Self), an argument whose parameter is an interface in all known overloads, and an assignment to an interface variable. High confidence. Quick fix in case 2: move the statement before inherited.

rules.name: Comparison with Null instead of VarIsNull or IsNull
rules.description: X = Null or X <> Null compares a variant with Null. The result depends on the global System.Variants.NullEqualityRule: with the default ncrLoose the comparison works as expected, with ncrStrict it is never true and with ncrError it raises an exception. A library, a test framework or another part of the project can change the rule. VarIsNull(X) and Field.IsNull check independently of it. Reported only where the comparison stands on its own (condition, argument, assignment); not X = Null binds as (not X) = Null and gets no quick fix. High confidence. Quick fix: Field.IsNull for X.Value on FieldByName, FindField, Fields[...], ParamByName, Params[...] or a field of type T...Field/T...Param, otherwise VarIsNull(X); with <> preceded by not.
rules.bad:
if qryKunde.FieldByName('Geburtstag').Value = Null then
  Alter := 0;
rules.good:
if qryKunde.FieldByName('Geburtstag').IsNull then
  Alter := 0;

rules.name: Number cast to enumeration without check
rules.description: TStatus(N) with an enumeration type declared in the file or the index, where N comes from a call listed in the option sources (FieldByName, ReadInteger, AsInteger, StrToInt): directly in the argument or via a variable that is not read (checked) between its assignment and the cast. A value outside the range yields an invalid enumeration value that falls through case statements. EnsureRange, Min or Max in the argument count as a check; constants, arithmetic and unknown types stay silent. For enumerations with explicit ordinal values the range is given as Ord(Low(T))..Ord(High(T)). Medium confidence. Quick fix for a direct source in a statement of its own: helper variable, InRange check with raise EConvertError before it, System.Math added to uses.
rules.bad: Status := TStatus(qry.FieldByName('Status').AsInteger);

options.name: sources
options.description: Calls whose result counts as unchecked.

rules.name: CreateProcess with a read-only command line
rules.description: CreateProcess (CreateProcessW) and CreateProcessAsUser write into the buffer of lpCommandLine. A PChar on memory that cannot be written causes an access violation. Reported for PChar(...)/PWideChar(...) on: a string literal or constant; a concatenation of exactly one literal and one value (if the value is empty, the RTL returns the literal itself); a local string variable whose last assignment before the call is one of these, without UniqueString afterwards; a string parameter (medium confidence, the caller may pass a literal). Function results such as Format and concatenations with several parts are writable heap strings and stay silent, as does CreateProcessA, which copies the command line itself. Quick fix: copy the command line into a local variable and call UniqueString; for a variable, UniqueString before the statement. No quick fix in loop conditions.
rules.bad: CreateProcess(nil, PChar('notepad.exe ' + Datei), nil, nil, False, 0, nil, nil, SI, PI);

rules.name: Access to a form that is not created yet
rules.description: The constructor, AfterConstruction or the OnCreate handler of an automatically created form or data module uses the global variable of another form that the .dpr creates later with Application.CreateForm. The variable is still nil at that point. The order comes from the .dpr of the project the unit belongs to; the OnCreate handler from the form file (FormCreate or DataModuleCreate without one). Silent when the routine checks the variable (Assigned, comparison with nil), assigns it itself, creates it with CreateForm or declares a local name of the same name, and for forms that are not created automatically. Each variable is reported once per routine. Medium confidence. No quick fix: change the order in the .dpr or move the access to OnShow.

rules.name: General exception handler before a specific one
rules.description: In a try..except with several on handlers the first matching handler wins. A handler for a class that an earlier handler already catches is never reached: its code is dead and the special treatment never runs. Reported when an earlier handler names the same class, an ancestor of it, Exception (covers every exception class) or TObject. Ancestors come from the unit, the project index and a table of known RTL, VCL and FireDAC exception classes (for example EStreamError > EFOpenError, EIntError > ERangeError); unknown classes are only compared with Exception and TObject. Quick fix: move the specific handler before the general one (only when both handlers stand on their own lines). A duplicate handler for the same class is reported without a quick fix.

rules.name: raise E instead of raise in a handler
rules.description: raise E; in an on E: … handler raises the caught exception object again as a new raise. The RTL does not free the object twice, but the exception now starts at the handler: ExceptAddr and the call stack of tools such as madExcept or JclDebug point to the handler instead of the original fault, and the original location is lost. raise; re-raises the current exception unchanged. Also reported for raise E at …, then without a quick fix. Silent when the handler takes the object over with AcquireExceptionObject or assigns a new object to the variable, inside anonymous methods and for handlers without a variable name. High confidence. Quick fix: raise E; → raise;.

rules.name: Blocking call in the main thread
rules.description: Sleep, WaitFor, WaitForSingleObject, WaitForMultipleObjects or Wait in methods of forms and frames (classes that inherit from TForm, TCustomForm, TFrame or TCustomFrame) and in event handlers (methods with a Sender parameter) outside thread classes. The user interface freezes while the call waits; if the other thread waits for Synchronize, the program hangs. WaitFor without a timeout on a variable names the risk of the Synchronize deadlock. Sleep, WaitForSingleObject and WaitForMultipleObjects count only without a receiver (or with Winapi.Windows), WaitFor and Wait only on a receiver. A literal timeout below maxSleepMs (Sleep(10), WaitForSingleObject(H, 0)) stays silent, except a short Sleep in a waiting loop without Application.ProcessMessages. Anonymous methods are skipped (TTask.Run, TThread.Queue), nested routines belong to their method. Medium confidence. No quick fix: move the work into TTask.Run and report the result with TThread.Queue.

options.name: maxSleepMs
options.description: Literal timeouts below this value (milliseconds) are not reported; a short Sleep in a waiting loop still is.

options.name: calls
options.description: Calls that block. Other names are reported regardless of their arguments.

rules.name: Thread loop without Terminated
rules.description: A while or repeat loop in TThread.Execute, or in a method of the thread class that is only called from there (also through other such methods, including nested routines), does not check Terminated. Terminate then has no effect, and WaitFor or Free hang when the program shuts down. Reported for endless loops (while True, until False) and for waiting loops with Sleep, WaitFor, WaitForSingleObject, WaitForMultipleObjects, MsgWaitForMultipleObjects, Wait or Yield whose condition and body never mention Terminated or CheckTerminated. Thread classes come from the unit and the index. Bounded loops, for loops, anonymous methods and classes that override TerminatedSet (they end their loops another way) stay silent. High confidence. Quick fix: add Terminated to the loop condition (while True → while not Terminated, otherwise and not Terminated; until False → until Terminated, otherwise or Terminated).

rules.name: Anonymous thread never started
rules.description: TThread.CreateAnonymousThread(…) creates the thread suspended with FreeOnTerminate set. Without Start the thread never runs, and because it never terminates it is never freed either. Reported for the call as a statement of its own and for a local variable (also an inline variable) that is never started with Start or Resume and not passed on (argument, assignment, Result, field). Setting properties such as FreeOnTerminate or OnTerminate does not count as passing on. High confidence. Quick fix: append .Start; for a variable, T.Start; after the last statement of the same block that mentions it.

rules.name: Exception in TTask gets lost
rules.description: TTask.Run(…) or TTask.Create(…).Start whose result is never kept or queried with Wait, Status or similar, and whose anonymous method has no try … except. An exception in the task disappears silently. Also reported for a local variable that is never mentioned again (for TTask.Create only in V.Start). Silent for kept results (fields, Result, any other use of the variable) and for method references, whose body the rule cannot see. Medium confidence. Quick fix: wrap the body in try … except and report the message on the main thread through TThread.Queue with ShowMessage (adds Vcl.Dialogs, or FMX.Dialogs in FireMonkey units, and System.SysUtils to the uses clause when missing); only when begin and end of the anonymous method stand on their own lines.

rules.name: Dataset loop without Next
rules.description: while not Q.Eof do without Q.Next in the body, or with Next only on some of the paths that continue the loop (an if without else, Continue before Next). The loop spins forever on the same record. Delete, MoveBy, Last, Close, FindNext and Free also count as moving on; Break, Exit, Abort and raise end the loop. Nested while and for loops are not trusted to run. When Q is passed on in the body (argument, assignment, with), the called code may move the record pointer and the rule stays silent. High confidence when Next is missing entirely, medium when only some paths miss it. Quick fix: insert Q.Next; at the end of the begin … end body (only when Next is missing entirely).

rules.name: Edit or Append without Post
rules.description: After Edit, Append or Insert (without arguments) on a dataset, the same routine calls neither Post nor Cancel (nor CheckBrowseMode). The change stays open and is silently lost on scrolling or saved unexpectedly later; on an exception in between, nothing cancels it. Silent when another routine of the unit posts or cancels the same dataset (an Edit button with a separate Save button) and when the dataset is passed on after Edit (argument, assignment, with). Medium confidence. Quick fix: wrap the following statements that use the dataset in try … except, with Post at the end of the try part and Cancel; raise; in the except part.

rules.name: Transaction without Rollback
rules.description: StartTransaction without Rollback in the except part of the try that directly follows. On an exception the transaction stays open and holds locks. Recognized for FireDAC (TFDConnection, TFDTransaction), IBX and dbExpress (StartTransaction/Commit/Rollback), dbExpress from XE (BeginTransaction/CommitFreeAndNil/RollbackFreeAndNil, also as T := Conn.BeginTransaction) and ADO (BeginTrans/CommitTrans/RollbackTrans). The option pairs replaces these pairs with your own. The Rollback may sit in a try … except inside a try … finally that follows directly. Silent when another routine of the unit rolls back the same connection (transaction across several events). High confidence. Quick fix: wrap the statements up to the Commit of the same block in try … except with Rollback (with the arguments of the Commit) and raise; only when a Commit follows in the same block.

options.name: pairs
options.description: Transaction methods per library as [{"start": …, "commit": …, "rollback": …}]; replaces the built-in pairs.

rules.name: UPDATE or DELETE without WHERE
rules.description: An UPDATE or DELETE without WHERE in a string literal, SQL.Text, SQL.Add, CommandText, the first argument of ExecSQL, ExecSQLScalar, Open, ExecuteDirect or Execute, or in SQL.Strings/CommandText of the form file. It affects every row of the table; usually the condition was forgotten. The rule assembles the SQL text per query within a routine (Clear and a new Text start over) and substitutes constants and local values. JOIN, TOP, LIMIT and ROWS restrict the rows as well; a WHERE in a subquery or comment does not count. Unknown parts behind the table name (variables, calls at the place of a clause) keep the statement silent; a dynamic table name reports with medium confidence. Silent when the routine passes the SQL on or another routine of the unit adds to it; form file SQL only counts when the unit does not change it. Literals outside SQL properties count only with DELETE or UPDATE in capitals, so message texts stay silent. High confidence, no quick fix; tables that are emptied on purpose go into allowTables.
rules.bad:
qry.SQL.Text := 'DELETE FROM Warenkorb';
qry.ExecSQL;

options.name: allowTables
options.description: Tables that are deliberately emptied or changed completely, with or without schema.

rules.name: Implementation differs from declaration
rules.description: The header in the implementation section has different parameters (count, name, type, const/var/out), a different result type, procedure instead of function or a different calling convention than the declaration in the type (like E2037). With overloads the nearest declaration is compared (parameter count, then types, names and modifiers); if that is not unique, declared-not-implemented and implemented-not-declared report both sides instead. A body may omit the parameter list, the result type and the calling convention. Methods inside {$IF} blocks are skipped; with include files the confidence is medium. Quick fix: align the implementation header with the declaration, or, as the second action, the declaration with the implementation (default values stay in the declaration). Off with refactoring.syncSignatures = false only removes the quick fixes.

rules.name: Interface method missing in the class
rules.description: A class lists an interface but does not implement all of its methods, including those of ancestor interfaces (like E2291). A method of the class with the same name but a different signature is reported at that method (like E2211). Methods inherited from ancestor classes, method resolution clauses (procedure IFoo.Bar = Baz) and properties with implements count; public TObject methods and IInterface methods of TInterfacedObject and similar RTL bases count as well. If the chain of ancestor classes ends at an unknown class or the interface is unknown, the rule stays silent. A method resolution clause for an interface the class does not list is reported too (like E2265). Classes inside {$IF} blocks are skipped. Quick fix: declare the missing methods and create empty bodies (not offered when a header differs).

rules.name: Unit in uses not found
rules.description: A unit in uses or contains is found neither in the project nor in the folders the compiler searches: folder of the using file, project folder, search paths and DCU output folder of the .dproj, library paths of the installation, each as .pas or .dcu and with every unit scope name in front (SysUtils → System.SysUtils); in packages also the units of the required packages (like F2613). Also reported: a file from in '…' that does not exist (F1026), a package from requires found neither as .dpk nor as .dcp (E2202), a unit that uses itself (F2092), and once a missing unit System, i.e. a missing library path, instead of one finding per unit (F1027). Entries inside {$IF} blocks are skipped; without a known installation, with an open macro in a search path or with a required package of unknown content the rule stays silent. The message names similar units. Quick fixes: use the unit with its namespace (Forms → Vcl.Forms) or a similarly written unit, or add the folder below the project that holds the unit to DCC_UnitSearchPath of the base configuration in the .dproj.
rules.bad:
uses
  System.SysUtils, Vcl.Forms, Kunden.Daten, Rechnungs.Druck;
rules.good:
uses
  System.SysUtils, Vcl.Forms, Kunden.Daten, Rechnung.Druck;

options.name: searchPaths
options.description: Where units are searched: project (like the compiler: project, search paths of the .dproj, library paths, .pas and .dcu), atlas (what Atlas knows: index and browsing paths of the installation) or both.

rules.name: Attribute not found and silently ignored
rules.description: An attribute [Name] resolves neither to a class NameAttribute nor to Name, usually because a unit is missing in uses. Delphi only warns (W1074) and skips the attribute: DUnitX tests do not run, JSON or ORM mappings are missing. The message names the unit that declares the attribute in the index; a facade unit that passes the type on from another candidate (DUnitX.TestFramework instead of DUnitX.Attributes) comes first, and the DUnitX attributes are known even without DUnitX in the index. Compiler attributes such as Weak, Unsafe, Ref and Volatile always count. Silent without the unit System in the index, when a unit from uses is not in the index (it could declare the attribute), inside {$IF} blocks and when an ancestor of the surrounding class is unknown; with include files the confidence is medium. Quick fix: add the unit to uses.
rules.bad:
uses
  System.SysUtils;
type
  [TestFixture]
  TKundeTests = class
rules.good:
uses
  System.SysUtils, DUnitX.TestFramework;
type
  [TestFixture]
  TKundeTests = class

rules.name: Comparison instead of assignment as a statement
rules.description: A comparison such as Result = 0; or FAktiv = True; stands on its own as a statement; := was meant. Delphi only reports E2014 when compiling. With = and an assignable left side (variable, field, element, pointer target) the quick fix replaces = with :=. Other comparisons and expressions whose value is discarded (A <> B;, A + B;, not A;, a literal) are reported without a fix, as is a call on the left side.
rules.bad: Result = 0;
rules.good: Result := 0;

rules.name: Duplicate case label
rules.description: Two labels of a case statement cover the same value (like E2030), also through ranges (1..5 and 3), constants with the same value, characters ('a' and #97) and enumeration ranges. The same applies to the labels of a variant record part (like E2027). Values are computed from numbers, characters, constants and enumeration values via name resolution; labels whose value is unknown are only compared by their text. A label is only reported when the earlier one is compiled whenever it is: different branches of the same {$IF} never clash. Quick fix: remove the duplicate value from the later branch, or the whole branch when it was its only label; a partial range overlap is reported without a fix.

rules.name: Field after methods in the same section
rules.description: Within a visibility section of a class, object or record, a field declaration follows a method or property. Delphi requires fields first or a new section or var (E2169); FPC accepts it. Quick fixes: move the field with its attributes and comments to the start of the section, or put var in front of it. In records var comes first because moving changes the memory layout. A field is only reported when a method before it is compiled whenever the field is; with conditional branches in between only var is offered.

rules.name: Overload without overload or with the same signature
rules.description: Two routines or methods of the same name in the same scope (a type, the unit across interface and implementation, the routines nested in a routine), of which at least one lacks overload (like E2254, or E2267 when the earlier one lacks it), or two overloads with the same parameter kinds and types (like E2252, or E2301 with the same result type as well). A body that implements an earlier declaration (interface, forward) does not count. Operators, method bodies and declarations in different branches of the same {$IF} are skipped. Quick fix: append overload; to every declaration without it, before the other directives.
rules.bad:
procedure Laden(const Datei: string);
procedure Laden(Strom: TStream);
rules.good:
procedure Laden(const Datei: string); overload;
procedure Laden(Strom: TStream); overload;

rules.name: Identifier declared twice
rules.description: An identifier is declared twice in the same scope (like E2004): a local variable, constant, type or label and a parameter of the routine, two fields, a field and a method or property of a type, two types, a constant and a variable of the unit across interface and implementation. Likewise a unit twice in uses or in the uses clauses of interface and implementation at once (option checkUses). Overloads and bodies of routines, a forward declaration and its type, TList next to TList<T> and declarations in different branches of the same {$IF} do not count. Quick fix: remove the second declaration (the whole var, const, type or label section when it was its only one; for uses the duplicate entry); none for parameters, methods and properties.
rules.good:
procedure TRechnung.Summieren(Betrag: Currency);
begin

options.name: checkUses
options.description: Report duplicate entries in uses clauses.

rules.name: Conditional directives incomplete or unknown
rules.description: An {$IFDEF}, {$IFNDEF}, {$IFOPT} or {$IF} that is never closed, so the rest of the file depends on its condition (like E2095, E2280 for {$IF}); {$ELSE}, {$ELSEIF}, {$ENDIF} or {$IFEND} without a matching {$IF…}, or after {$ELSE} (like E2279); {$IFDEF}, {$IFNDEF}, {$DEFINE} or {$UNDEF} without a valid symbol (like E2173); an unknown directive or {$WARN} identifier (like W1030), with the closest known name as quick fix; {$POPOPT} without {$PUSHOPT} (like W1078) or {$PUSHOPT} without {$POPOPT} (like W1079); an invalid value for {$ALIGN} or {$A} (like E2573). Unknown names are not checked in branches whose condition tests FPC, {$PUSHOPT}/{$POPOPT} only when none of them is inside a conditional branch. Quick fixes: add {$ENDIF} before the first blank line after the open block, remove a surplus directive, correct the typo.

rules.name: override without a matching virtual method
rules.description: A method marked override for which no ancestor has a virtual (or dynamic, abstract) method with the same name and parameters (like E2137): often a typo (Destory) or parameters changed in the ancestor. The message names the closest virtual method of the ancestor ("there it is Ausfuehren(const Modus: TModus)") or a similar name. Also: override on a static method (like E2170), on a final one (like E2352), and deriving from a sealed class (like E2353). Ancestors are looked up in the file and in the symbol index; when the chain breaks at an unknown class the rule stays silent. Without System in the index the virtual methods of TObject count as present. Type parameters of generic ancestors, type aliases and synonyms such as Longint match. Quick fix: take over the ancestor's signature in the declaration and the implementation.

rules.name: Instance of a class with abstract methods
rules.description: Create on a class that declares or inherits abstract methods without overriding them (like W1020), or on a class declared abstract (like E2402). Calling an abstract method raises EAbstractError at run time; the message names the open methods. Classes are looked up in the file and in the symbol index; overloads with the same number of parameters count as one method. Calls on class references, inherited Create and constructor bodies are not checked. Quick fix for a class of this file that inherits the abstract methods: override them there (like the code action "override").
rules.bad:
Form := TForm.Create;
Gesamt := Gesamt + Form.Flaeche;
rules.good:
Form := TKreis.Create;
Gesamt := Gesamt + Form.Flaeche;

rules.name: Invalid property getter or setter
rules.description: The name after read or write of a property does not fit: it is declared neither in the class nor in its ancestors, or it is a property (like E2168); the getter or setter has the wrong kind, parameters or types (like E2234); the setter takes a var or out parameter (like E2282); the accessor is overloaded and no overload fits (like E2271); a class property uses an instance member or a class method without static (like E2355), or an instance property uses a class var or a static class method (like E2356); an array property uses a field (like E2174, index with a field compiles); a field selector goes through a field that is no record (like E2459), names a member that is no field (like E2461) or a field the record lacks (like E2562). Names are looked up in the file and, for ancestors, in the symbol index; the rule stays silent when the ancestor chain breaks, the name only exists in an inactive branch, the class cannot see it or the class includes files. Types are compared only when both are built in or declared as types of their own. Quick fix for a missing F<Name>, Get<Name> or Set<Name>: create it (like the completion after read/write, completion.accessorSection).

rules.name: Assignment to a field of a property record
rules.description: Assignment to a field of a record that a property with a getter, a default or array property or a function result only delivers as a copy (like E2064): the assignment has no effect. Assignments to untyped constants are reported as well. Types come from name resolution; the rule only reports when the record type is known for sure. A property that reads a field directly lets Delphi write into that field and stays silent. Quick fix for a property with write: assign through a local variable and write it back; the variable is declared in the routine and the unit of its type is added to uses.
rules.bad: Rahmen.BoundsRect.Left := 0;

rules.name: Assignment to a property without write
rules.description: Assignment to a property that has no write (like E2129), or reading a property that has no read (like E2130). The rule only reports when name resolution finds the property for sure; redeclarations without read and write (property Caption;) count as unknown. Quick fixes: Count := 0 becomes Clear when the type has Clear; inside a method of the declaring class, assign the field behind read; for a property declared in this file, create the setter and add write.
rules.bad: Liste.Count := 0;
rules.good: Liste.Clear;

rules.name: SELECT * in code
rules.description: SELECT * or SELECT alias.* in a column list, in the same places as sql-write-without-where: string literals, SQL.Text, SQL.Add, CommandText, the first argument of ExecSQL, Open and similar calls, constants, local values and SQL.Strings/CommandText of the form file. New columns silently change the dataset, persistent fields no longer match, and more data is transferred than needed. Subqueries count; EXISTS (SELECT * …) and COUNT(*) stay silent, as does a column list from a variable. Literals outside SQL properties count only with SELECT in capitals and a FROM, so message texts stay silent. Off by default (enable in the rules settings or with the strict profile). High confidence. Quick fix: when the star stands in a single literal and the dataset has persistent fields in the form file, replace * with their FieldName list (without calculated and lookup fields).
rules.bad: qry.SQL.Text := 'SELECT * FROM Kunden WHERE Ort = :Ort';
rules.good: qry.SQL.Text := 'SELECT Id, Name, Ort FROM Kunden WHERE Ort = :Ort';

rules.name: Path joined without delimiter
rules.description: A folder without a trailing path delimiter is joined to a file or folder name with +: results of ExtractFileDir, ExcludeTrailingPathDelimiter, GetCurrentDir, GetHomePath, TPath.GetDocumentsPath and the other TPath.Get…Path folders, TPath.GetDirectoryName, TDirectory.GetCurrentDirectory and TDirectory.GetParent, called directly or held in a local variable that the routine only assigns such values to. The result is C:\Datadatei.txt instead of C:\Data\datei.txt. ExtractFilePath, IncludeTrailingPathDelimiter and TPath.GetTempPath end with a delimiter and stay silent, as do delimiters, extensions (ExtractFileExt, '.bak') and texts that start with a space or punctuation. A literal name reports with high confidence, an identifier with medium confidence. A local variable passed to a procedure other than ForceDirectories, FileExists and similar read-only calls may be changed there and stays silent. Quick fix: TPath.Combine(Folder, Name), adding System.IOUtils to uses.
rules.bad:
Ordner := TPath.GetDocumentsPath;
Datei := Ordner + 'export.csv';
rules.good:
Ordner := TPath.GetDocumentsPath;
Datei := TPath.Combine(Ordner, 'export.csv');

rules.name: Hard-coded file path
rules.description: A string literal with a drive letter (C:\…, also with /) or a UNC path (\\server\share\…); paths under C:\Users or C:\Documents and Settings get their own message. On other computers the path is missing. Drive roots such as 'C:\' alone and the prefixes \\?\ and \\.\ stay silent, as do comments, test units and units listed in allowUnits (for example a unit with the default paths of an installation). High confidence, no quick fix: take the path from TPath (GetDocumentsPath, GetHomePath, GetSharedDocumentsPath), the settings or an environment variable.
rules.bad: Protokoll.SaveToFile('C:\Users\marco\Desktop\log.txt');
rules.good: Protokoll.SaveToFile(TPath.Combine(TPath.GetDocumentsPath, 'log.txt'));

options.name: allowUnits
options.description: Units in which hard-coded paths are allowed, by unit name; * at the end matches a prefix (App.Config*).

rules.name: File names compared with =
rules.description: A comparison with = or <> where one side is a file or path name: the result of ExtractFileName, ExtractFilePath, ExtractFileDir, ExtractFileExt, ExpandFileName, ChangeFileExt and related System.SysUtils functions, of TPath.GetFileName, GetExtension, GetDirectoryName, GetFullPath, Combine and related methods, or a variable or property whose name ends in FileName, or Application.ExeName. On Windows Kunde.pas and kunde.PAS are the same file. Comparisons with an empty string, nil or a literal without letters stay silent, as does ExtractFileDir(X) = X (both sides come from the same text). Medium confidence. Quick fix: SameFileName(A, B), or not SameFileName(A, B) for <>; adds System.SysUtils to uses if needed.
rules.bad: if ExtractFileName(Datei) = 'Config.ini' then
rules.good: if SameFileName(ExtractFileName(Datei), 'Config.ini') then

rules.name: Object created at startup is not freed
rules.description: An object is created with TClass.Create in the initialization section and assigned to a unit variable, or created in a class constructor and assigned to a class var, but the unit never frees it (no Free, Destroy, DisposeOf, Release or FreeAndNil anywhere in the unit). FastMM reports a leak on shutdown; in packages the object stays behind on every unload. Interface and record types, components with an owner (Application, Self, Owner) and objects the unit hands over stay silent: every mention of the variable must be harmless (member access, comparison with nil, Assigned, a new Create or nil assignment); passing it as an argument, assigning it elsewhere, with, a property reading it or FreeOnTerminate silence the rule. For variables in the interface section and public class vars the rule also stays silent when another indexed unit uses the name. High confidence. Quick fix: FreeAndNil at the end of finalization or in the class destructor; a missing finalization section or class destructor (declaration and body) is created and System.SysUtils is added to uses when needed.

rules.name: Compiler warnings or checks switched off up to the end of the unit
rules.description: {$WARNINGS OFF}, {$HINTS OFF}, {$WARN X OFF}, {$R-}, {$Q-} (also combined as {$R-,Q-}) or the long forms {$RANGECHECKS OFF} and {$OVERFLOWCHECKS OFF} without a later restore up to the end of the unit. Messages and checks disappear far beyond the intended spot, and the 0/0/0 rule is bypassed. Any later ON, +, DEFAULT or ERROR for the same switch counts as a restore, also inside {$IFOPT}/{$IFDEF} patterns, as does a later {$POPOPT}. A switch whose counterpart stands in another branch of the same {$IF} ({$IFDEF DEBUG}{$R+}{$ELSE}{$R-}{$ENDIF}) is a deliberate setting per configuration and stays silent, as does a directive with no code after it; {$R *.dfm} is a resource, not a range check. Option allow lists switches that may stay off (warning names such as SYMBOL_PLATFORM, WARNINGS, HINTS, R or RANGECHECKS, Q or OVERFLOWCHECKS). High confidence. Quick fix: insert the restore ({$WARNINGS ON}, {$WARN X DEFAULT}, {$R+} …) after the next block; for range and overflow checks only individually, since {$R+} may switch on a check the project has off.

options.name: allow
options.description: Switches that may stay off up to the end of the unit: warning names for {$WARN} (SYMBOL_PLATFORM), WARNINGS, HINTS, R or RANGECHECKS, Q or OVERFLOWCHECKS; case is ignored.

rules.name: Exported routine not safe across DLL boundaries
rules.description: A routine of this file listed in exports has no calling convention (stdcall, cdecl, safecall, winapi or pascal; register is the Delphi convention) or takes or returns a string (string, UnicodeString, AnsiString, UTF8String, RawByteString), a dynamic array (TBytes, TArray<T>, …DynArray, array of T declared in the file), an object or an interface without GUID. Callers in other languages or Delphi versions crash; strings and dynamic arrays live in the memory manager of the DLL. WideString, ShortString, PChar, open array parameters and records are fine. Objects are only recognised for certain: classes of the file, of the index and common RTL classes; interfaces only from the file. Routines from other units and overloads that the exports entry does not pin down stay silent. With ShareMem or SimpleShareMem in uses, strings and dynamic arrays are allowed (option allowShareMem). The finding sits on the exports entry; for strings it recommends PChar with buffer and length. High confidence. Quick fix: add stdcall to every header of the routine (only individually, since it changes the interface for existing callers).

options.name: allowShareMem
options.description: With ShareMem or SimpleShareMem in uses, strings and dynamic arrays are allowed in exported routines.

rules.name: Destructor uses fields that may be nil
rules.description: If a constructor raises, Delphi calls the destructor right away, even though not all fields exist yet. Reported is an access in the destructor (or in a private method that only the destructor calls) to a field such as FLines.Clear, FFile.Position or FLines[0], when a constructor of the class creates the field (TClass.Create) only after a call that can raise or only on some paths. The resulting access violation hides the original exception. Free, FreeAndNil, DisposeOf and accesses after Assigned(FField) or FField <> nil are nil-safe; BeforeDestruction does not run on this path. Constructors of RTL classes that raise at most EOutOfMemory (TStringList.Create, TObjectList<T>.Create(True)), inherited Create and Supports do not count as raising. High confidence. Quick fix: put if Assigned(FField) then in front of the statement. With onlyAfterRaisingCode off, every field created in the constructor counts.

options.name: onlyAfterRaisingCode
options.description: Only report when the constructor calls something that can raise before it creates the field.

rules.name: Windows handle is not closed
rules.description: A Windows handle in a local variable is not closed with its counterpart on some path to the end of the routine: CreateFile, CreateEvent, CreateMutex, OpenProcess, CreateProcess (hProcess, hThread) and CreateToolhelp32Snapshot with CloseHandle, FindFirstFile with FindClose, RegOpenKeyEx/RegCreateKeyEx with RegCloseKey, LoadLibrary with FreeLibrary, GetDC with ReleaseDC, CreatePen/CreateBrush/CreateFont/CreateBitmap with DeleteObject, CreateCompatibleDC with DeleteDC and others. Returning the handle, storing it in a field or global, passing it to an unknown routine or capturing it in an anonymous method counts as handing it on. Branches in which an if check says the open failed (H = 0, H = INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE, RegOpenKeyEx(...) <> ERROR_SUCCESS) and exception paths (see pair-without-finally) do not count. The option pairs adds your own pairs. Medium confidence. Quick fix when the handle is never closed: wrap the statements after the open in try … finally with the close call, or append the close call when the open is the last statement.

options.name: pairs
options.description: Additional open/close pairs as "Open>Close" or {"open": …, "close": …}; the open function returns the handle, the close procedure takes it as its only argument.

rules.name: Global FormatSettings is modified
rules.description: Assignment to the global FormatSettings or one of its fields (also to the deprecated global variables DecimalSeparator, ShortDateFormat, ThousandSeparator … of older Delphi versions). This changes the formatting for the whole application, for every package in the same process (in an IDE plugin the IDE itself) and for all threads, and is not thread-safe; it is often a workaround to force a dot as decimal separator. Reported only when the name is surely the variable from System.SysUtils: no local declaration, no member of the class or its ancestors (silent when the chain of ancestors ends at an unknown class), not inside with. Complements format-without-settings, which reports formatting calls without settings. High confidence. Quick fix when the routine changes the global settings only once and formats something afterwards: declare a local TFormatSettings (TFormatSettings.Invariant for DecimalSeparator := '.', otherwise a copy of FormatSettings with the changed field) and pass it to the formatting calls that follow. With allowInProgram on, assignments in the .dpr are allowed.

options.name: allowInProgram
options.description: Allow the assignments in the .dpr, for example once at program start.

rules.name: Component stored as interface stays referenced after Free
rules.description: A descendant of TComponent (form, frame, data module, own component) implements an interface, but TComponent does not count references. Reported is storing the object as an interface in a field, a global variable or a list (FView as IObserver passed to Bus.Subscribe, FList.Add, Register, Anmelden …, assigned to a field or global, or added to a TList<IFoo>/TInterfaceList) when the same unit frees the object (Free, Release, DisposeOf, FreeAndNil) and nowhere unregisters it: FreeNotification on the object, another call on the same receiver with the object as argument (Unsubscribe, Remove, Abmelden …), Clear, or another assignment to the same field. After the Free the stored interface points to freed memory. Silent for classes with their own _Release and when the chain of ancestors ends at an unknown class. Also reported, without a quick fix: descendants of TInterfacedObject that are stored this way and additionally freed with Free; the stored interface keeps a freed object, and unregistering first would already free it. Medium confidence. Quick fix: insert the unregistration before the first Free (Receiver.Abmelden(…) when the receiver's type has the counterpart, or Field := nil).

options.name: componentClasses
options.description: Base classes without reference counting; with TComponent the known VCL and FMX classes (TForm, TFrame, TDataModule …) count as well.

rules.name: Unit name does not match the file name
rules.description: The name after unit differs from the file name, usually after renaming the file outside the IDE (like E1038, W1038). Case does not matter, dots in the name do. In a program, library or package, an entry uses X in 'File.pas' whose file declares a different unit is reported too (like E2085); the rule reads that file. Programs, libraries and packages themselves are not compared with their file name, because the compiler does not either. {$WARN UNIT_NAME_MISMATCH OFF} or {$WARNINGS OFF} before the unit name silences the rule like the compiler. Quick fixes: change the unit name to the file name (renaming the file is up to the IDE), or change the uses entry to the unit the file declares.

rules.name: Text after the final end.
rules.description: Source code after the final end. of a unit, program, library or package. The compiler ignores it (like W1011); usually it is code that ended up at the end of the file while pasting and is never compiled. Comments and directives are not reported (option allowComments). The rule finds the final end. behind the last section of the syntax tree and stays silent while the parser reports errors or when end. is inside an {$IF…} branch; {$WARNINGS OFF} before end. silences it. Quick fix: remove the text after end.
rules.good: end.

options.name: allowComments
options.description: Allow comments and directives after end.

rules.name: Invalid exports clause
rules.description: An exports clause inside a routine (like E2191), the export of a threadvar or of a routine declared local (like E2276), of a variable, constant or type (like E2121), or the same entry or export name twice (like E2287). Names are only resolved against global declarations of the file; names from other units and names with a dot stay silent, as do two entries in mutually exclusive {$IF…} branches. Overloaded routines with different parameter lists or export names count as different entries. Complements dll-export-unsafe (#973). Quick fix: remove the duplicate entry.
rules.bad:
exports
  Initialisieren,
  Berechnen,
  Initialisieren;

rules.name: Unit name conflicts
rules.description: A unit is named like a unit reserved for the compiler, System or SysInit (like E2272), or {$NOINCLUDE X} names a unit the compiler does not know (like E2242); the latter needs the project's unit search and stays silent when it gives no sure answer. The RTL sources (source/rtl) are not checked. Not reported: E2447, W1051 and X2421 belong to the namespaces of .NET metadata, which dcc32/dcc64 do not create; for E2399 the documentation gives no condition, and a unit Kunden next to Kunden.Daten compiles without error in Delphi (Spring.pas next to Spring.Collections.pas). Quick fix for {$NOINCLUDE}: use a similarly spelled known unit.
rules.bad:
unit System;

interface
rules.good:
unit Kunden.Systemdienste;

interface

rules.name: Variant without System.Variants in uses
rules.description: The unit uses Variant or OleVariant as a type without System.Variants in uses. The compiler then adds the unit silently (like W1040) and so changes the initialization order. The rule counts type references in the syntax tree (variables, fields, parameters, results, type arguments); Variants in uses also counts inside an {$IF…} branch and without namespace. Silent in System, SysInit and Variants themselves, when the file declares its own type Variant, and after {$WARN IMPLICIT_VARIANTS OFF}. Off by default (strict profile). Quick fix: add System.Variants to uses (Variants when the unit names SysUtils or Classes without namespace).

rules.name: Encoding or character the compiler does not read
rules.description: The file is UTF-32 encoded (like F2438; recognized by its byte order mark, no further findings then), or the code outside strings, comments and directives contains a character the compiler rejects (like E2038): typographic quotes copied from a web page or a word processor, the ASCII characters ! " ? \ ` | ~ and punctuation, symbols and emoji beyond ASCII. Letters, digits and connectors such as U+203F stay allowed in identifiers; asm blocks and {$IF…} branches are skipped; control, format and space characters are left to control-char and invisible-char. Quick fix: a pair of quotes on one line becomes a string literal; a single character with an unambiguous ASCII counterpart (– − × ÷ ≤ ≥ ≠, full-width ASCII) is replaced. A UTF-32 file has no quick fix; save it as UTF-8 with BOM.
rules.bad: Titel := ‚Bericht‘;
rules.good: Titel := 'Bericht';

rules.name: Anonymous method captures what it must not capture
rules.description: An anonymous method uses a var, out or untyped parameter, or Result, of a surrounding routine or anonymous function (like E2555). The name is resolved from the inside out (parameters, var/const/type, local routines, inline variables, for var); inside with and asm the rule stays silent, and declarations in conditional branches that exclude the location do not count. Quick fix: copy the value into a local variable before the statement, use only that variable in the anonymous method, and write it back after the statement when the method assigns it.

rules.name: Operator declared incorrectly
rules.description: A class operator in a record or class is declared in a way Delphi rejects: unknown operator name (like E2393), wrong number of parameters (E2517), own type missing from the parameters (E2518) or from parameters and result for Implicit/Explicit (E2521), Inc/Dec with a result type other than the first parameter (E2519), conversion to or from an ancestor (E2522, chain within the file) or Assign without var before the first parameter (E2464). Types count as equal when their names match without unit prefix and type arguments; aliases of the own type declared in the file keep the rule silent, and True, False and OnesComplement are accepted. Comparison operators with a result other than Boolean compile (Spring4D criteria) and stay silent. Quick fixes: nearest operator name, result like the first parameter, var before the first parameter, parameter list from the template; each in the declaration and the implementation.

rules.name: Generic declaration not allowed
rules.description: A generic declaration that Delphi rejects: class and record constraints together (like E2507), a constraint twice (E2603), record together with constructor (E2516), a class type next to class or record (E2552), two class types (E2553), a constraint type that is neither class nor interface (E2510); type parameters on an enumeration, set, subrange, pointer, class reference, alias or helper (E2508), on a destructor or class constructor (E2528), an operator (E2529), a global routine (E2530), a virtual, dynamic, message or override method (E2533) or an interface method (E2535); class of a parameterized type (E2548), a generic class derived from TCustomAttribute (E2549), a parameterized type as attribute (E2565); a type parameter that hides one of the enclosing type (H2509); a call with a number of type arguments no overload has (E2551, classes and records of the file with their ancestors in the file); a method of a generic type or a generic method declared in the interface section that uses a symbol of the implementation section (E2506; silent inside with and when the ancestor chain is not known). Types count only when they are built in or declared in the file; unknown types keep the rule silent. Local procedures in generic methods (E2570) are not reported until a check against Delphi 12/13 confirms that they are still rejected.
rules.bad: procedure Swap<T>(var A, B: T);

rules.name: Language rule for records, inline and helpers violated
rules.description: Fixed language rules that only the compiler reports: virtual methods (like E2379) or other virtual directives (override, abstract, reintroduce, message, final; E2463) in records, parameterless constructors (E2394), constructors whose parameters all have defaults (E2471) and destructors (E2465) in records, class methods in records without static (E2398); in record helpers virtual methods (E2598) and the other virtual directives (E2475); fields in helpers (class var is allowed, E2599), a destructor in a class helper (E2295; class constructors and helper constructors without a constructor call compile, Skia4Delphi), a class helper descending from a helper whose type the new target does not descend from (E2294, only with a known ancestor chain), a helper used as type of a declaration (E2527) or declared inside a generic type (E2589); several class constructors (E2359, exclusive conditional branches count once), class constructors with parameters (E2360) or virtual, dynamic or message (E2534); methods, properties, class members, types and constants in local or anonymous records (E2433 to E2437); inline on virtual or dynamic methods (E2425), on constructors and destructors (E2442), with open array parameters (E2439), with an asm body (E2426), declared in the interface section and using a variable or typed constant of the implementation section (E2441; true constants, enumeration values, types and routines compile, mORMot2, Clipper2, dcc run of 29.10.2026), as local routine reading variables of the enclosing routine (E2449) or calling its own local routines (E2501); local, absolute or initialized threadvar (E2189, E2190, E2194). The checks apply to all supported Delphi versions (10 Seattle to 13). Option disabledChecks leaves out single codes. Quick fixes: remove the directive, add static.

options.name: disabledChecks
options.description: Compiler codes the rule does not check, e.g. ["E2425"].

rules.name: Attribute used incorrectly
rules.description: A compiler attribute is used where Delphi rejects it: [Weak] on a field or variable whose type is certainly neither a class nor an interface (built-in value types, records, enumerations, sets, arrays, pointer types of the file, aliases followed; like E2584), [Volatile] on a type, routine, method or property (E2325), Weak, Unsafe, Volatile or Ref twice on the same declaration (E2326; branches that exclude each other do not count), or an attribute argument that is certainly a variable or a routine of the file (E2448; visible before the attribute, not shadowed by a constant, type or other declaration of the same name). Custom attributes may be repeated; a type Weak or WeakAttribute declared in the file keeps the rule silent for that name. No quick fix.

rules.name: TypeInfo or Default with an invalid argument
rules.description: TypeInfo or Default receives a variable instead of a type (like E2133, E2537: parameters, local, inline and unit variables, fields, properties, Result, for and exception variables), TypeInfo receives a type without RTTI (enumeration with explicit values, file type, Text/TextFile; E2134), or Default receives a file type (E2538). Names are resolved from the inside out; inside with, in helpers, in methods of types outside the file, for declarations in other conditional branches and when the file or the index declares its own TypeInfo or Default the rule stays silent. Quick fix: insert the variable's declared type.
rules.bad: Name := GetEnumName(TypeInfo(Status), Ord(Status));
rules.good: Name := GetEnumName(TypeInfo(TStatus), Ord(Status));

rules.name: Condition or loop without begin … end
rules.description: The body of if … then, else, for, while or with is a single statement without begin … end. With the rule, conditions and loops always have a block, so a second statement added later does not end up outside by accident. else if stays allowed (the inner if needs no block of its own); repeat … until, case … end, try … end and asm … end are blocks already. An empty statement (if X then ;) is reported by empty-statement. Bodies with {$IFDEF} are not reported. While the rule is on, redundant-begin-end reports nothing. Quick fixes: put begin … end around the statement, for the whole method or for the whole file, indented by the format settings; a ; before else moves into the block (no E2153); with format.elsePlacement "sameLine", else follows the new end on the same line (end else).
rules.bad:
if Kunde.Gesperrt then
  Protokoll.Warnung('Gesperrt')
else
  Speichern(Kunde);

options.name: statements
options.description: Checked statements; add case for the branches of case statements.

options.name: allowSingleLineExit
options.description: Allow Exit, Continue, Break and raise on the same line as the condition (if … then Exit;).

options.name: allowSameLine
options.description: Allow a single statement on the same line as the condition or loop header.

rules.name: Inherited constructor only inside try
rules.description: A constructor enters a try block before it has called the inherited constructor (like H2505). Self is not initialised there yet; an exception in the block can hit half-created fields. Calls count as the inherited constructor when they are inherited without a name, with the constructor's own name or with a name starting with Create. Branches of {$IFDEF} are checked separately. Quick fix when the call is the first statement of the try block: move it before try.

rules.name: Managed type in the variant part of a record
rules.description: The variant part of a record (case … of) holds a string, dynamic array, interface, Variant or a record with such fields (like E2154), a custom managed record with class operator Initialize or Finalize (like E2418), or a type parameter without record constraint (like E2569); likewise after file of (like E2155, E2417). Types are resolved in the file and the index; unknown types stay silent. Quick fixes: move the field before case into the fixed part, use ShortString, or constrain the type parameter with record.

rules.name: GUID with invalid syntax
rules.description: The GUID of an interface or of a typed TGUID constant is not of the form '{8-4-4-4-12}' (like E2204): missing braces, wrong number or length of blocks, characters that are not hex digits, often after editing by hand. Only single literals are checked; concatenations and constants stay silent. Quick fixes: generate a new GUID; when only the braces are missing, add them. Complements interface-guid and duplicate-interface-guid.
rules.bad:
ILogger = interface
  ['{6A1F3B2C-9D4E-4F5A-8B7C-1D2E3F4A5B6}']
rules.good:
ILogger = interface
  ['{6A1F3B2C-9D4E-4F5A-8B7C-1D2E3F4A5B6C}']

rules.name: Untyped pointer bypasses reference counting
rules.description: An interface is assigned through a typecast to Pointer (Pointer(FIntf) := P, like W1070). Reference counting does not take part: the object is freed too early or never. The rule reports only when name resolution knows the interface type for sure; strings (string, AnsiString …) are reported as well, with the note "dcc does not report this", since Delphi warns about them only under NEXTGEN. Fields that already carry [weak] or [unsafe] stay silent. Quick fixes for an interface field of this file with Pointer(Y) or nil on the right: mark the field [weak] or [unsafe] and assign without Pointer.
rules.bad: Pointer(FBesitzer) := Pointer(Besitzer);

rules.name: Type exceeds a size limit
rules.description: A static array or record is 2 GB or larger (like E2100), or an instance of a generic type of this file is (like E2543). Atlas computes a lower bound from the declarations: index ranges via constant expressions, constants and enumerations of the file, built-in types, records from the index; unknown parts count as 0, so the rule reports only for sure. Only the innermost type that crosses the limit is reported. E2419 (records over 1 MB) applies only to Delphi for .NET and is not reported. No quick fix; use a dynamic array or a pointer instead.
rules.bad: type TPuffer = array[0..High(Integer)] of Int64;
rules.good: type TPuffer = array of Int64;

rules.name: Comparison always true or always false
rules.description: A comparison of a variable, field, property or function result of a built-in integer type with a constant outside or at the edge of its value range (like W1021, W1022): Cardinal >= 0 is always true, Byte > 255 always false. Case labels outside the range of the case expression are reported as well (like W1018). The rule only reports when the type is known for sure and its declaration is always compiled together with the comparison. NativeInt, LongInt and their unsigned counterparts count with the widest range of all platforms; subrange types are not reported. Length(...) < 0 and Length(...) >= 0 are reported as well, although dcc does not warn there; the message says so.
rules.bad: while Rest >= 0 do  // Rest: Cardinal
rules.good: while Rest > 0 do

rules.name: Initializer of a constant does not match
rules.description: A typed constant or initialized variable of a static array type has more or fewer elements than its index range (like E2072), typically after adding a value to an enumeration (array[TStatus] of string); checked per dimension and for named array types of the file. Record constants whose fields are in a different order than declared are reported as well (like E2083). Index ranges: subranges with constant bounds, enumerations without own values, Boolean, Byte, Char and so on. Declarations with conditional directives count as unsure. Quick fixes: over an enumeration, add missing or remove surplus entries at their position (recognized by texts, identifiers and comments naming the value; otherwise appended and labelled as estimated), new strings get the text of the value name, other types a default value with a {TODO value} comment (#667); over other ranges, add the missing entries with a placeholder; put the fields in the order of the declaration.
rules.bad: StatusText: array[TStatus] of string = ('Neu', 'Offen', 'Geschlossen');  // TStatus has 4 values
rules.good: StatusText: array[TStatus] of string = ('Neu', 'Offen', 'Geschlossen', ''{stArchiviert});

rules.name: case or for without an ordinal type
rules.description: case over an expression that is not ordinal (like E2001): strings, floating point numbers, classes and interfaces; a for loop whose counter is not ordinal (like E2032); case labels and array bounds that are variables, fields, properties, parameters or typed constants instead of constants (like E2026). The rule only reports when the type is known for sure and its declaration is always compiled together with the statement. Quick fix for strings whose labels are all string literals: case IndexStr(S, [...]) of with the positions as labels, System.StrUtils is added to uses.
rules.bad: case Befehl of 'start': Starten; 'stop': Stoppen; end;  // Befehl: string
rules.good: case IndexStr(Befehl, ['start', 'stop']) of 0: Starten; 1: Stoppen; end;

rules.name: Pointer and character width of a string do not match
rules.description: PChar or PWideChar on an AnsiString, RawByteString or UTF8String, and PAnsiChar on a string, UnicodeString or WideString (like W1044): pointer and character width do not match, a typical mistake after the Unicode migration; the API then reads garbage or only the first character. The rule only reports when the type of the argument is known for sure and its declaration is always compiled together with the cast. string(PAnsiChar) converts correctly and a pointer to TBytes may be intended; both are not reported.
