Quick fixes: declare an own variable with the matching string type (PChar(Pfad) with Pfad: AnsiString becomes Pfad: string), wrap the argument in string(...) or AnsiString(...), use the matching pointer type.
rules.bad: var Pfad: AnsiString; ... DeleteFile(PChar(Pfad));
rules.good: var Pfad: string; ... DeleteFile(PChar(Pfad));

rules.name: Access to a member that is not visible
rules.description: Access A.B to a member that is not visible at that point: private or strict private of another unit or class (like E2361), protected or strict protected outside the declaring unit and its descendants (like E2362, E2389). Inside a class method or static method, an instance field, method or property of the class is not reachable (like E2124). A property that refers to a private member of an ancestor in the same unit is reported as a warning (like W1045). The rule only reports when name resolution knows the receiver and its type for sure and finds the member only without regard to visibility; protected members stay visible through a class declared in the same unit (TAccess(Control).Click). A private class constructor does not hide an inherited Create, and a class overload of a method stays reachable from a class method. Protected members reached through a generic receiver (TNode<T>) compile from generic code in other units as well (Spring4D); from non-generic code dcc reports E2362. Declarations in conditional branches, methods of helpers and nested types stay silent.

rules.name: Private member never used
rules.description: A private or strict private field, method, constant or property is never used in the unit (like H2219, which the compiler only reports for methods; fields too unless includeFields is off). Any occurrence of the name as an identifier counts as a use, also in inactive conditional branches and behind read/write; declarations and method headers do not. Exempt: methods with message, virtual, dynamic, override or abstract, methods of types that implement interfaces, constructors and destructors, members with attributes (RTTI), names from the form file and units with include files. Quick fix: remove the declaration (with its /// documentation) and the body of a method; not when several members share the declaration or the method is overloaded.

options.name: includeFields
options.description: Also report private fields that are never used (the compiler reports only methods).

rules.name: Public member never used in the project
rules.description: A public or published method, constant or property (optionally also protected members, fields and class variables), or a routine, constant, type or global variable of the interface section (option unitKinds) is used nowhere in the projects of the project group. The search is project-wide via the symbol index: only files whose index usages contain the name are parsed, and every occurrence is resolved by name resolution; an occurrence that cannot be resolved counts as a use. Names in form files (.dfm/.fmx) and in string literals count as uses. Considered used: interface implementations and members of interfaces, virtual, dynamic, override, abstract and message methods, constructors, destructors, operators, enumerators, default properties, implements, members with attributes, published members of TPersistent descendants (streaming), of classes registered with RegisterComponents, RegisterClass or RegisterClasses and of test fixtures, published methods while a form file cannot be read, property accessors, exported routines, class helpers, members of classes with an unknown ancestor. Silent while projects are loading or the index is incomplete, when a file cannot be read, for units with include files and for units of packages or libraries (external users) unless projectKinds allows them. For types, occurrences in their own declaration and in the bodies of their own methods (including the TType.Name header) do not count; types registered with RegisterComponents, RegisterClass or RegisterClasses count as used, and for attribute classes (XyzAttribute) the short form [Xyz] counts. deadCode.keepAttributes and deadCode.keepPatterns from the settings apply in addition to keepAttributes and keepPatterns. Quick fix: mark as intentionally public (lsp-ignore comment).
rules.good:
TExport = class
  public
    procedure ExportiereAlsJson; // called by TMainForm
  end;

options.name: visibilities
options.description: Visibilities that are checked: public, published, protected.

options.name: memberKinds
options.description: Member kinds of types that are checked: method, constant, property, field, classVar. Unit-level declarations follow unitKinds.

options.name: projectKinds
options.description: Project kinds whose units are checked: application, package, library. Packages and libraries have users outside the project group, so they are off by default.

options.name: unitLevel
options.description: Also check declarations of the interface section of a unit (kinds from unitKinds).

options.name: unitKinds
options.description: Unit-level kinds that are checked with unitLevel: routine, constant, type, variable. Helpers are never reported (they are used through the extended type).

options.name: scope
options.description: Where uses are searched: projectGroup (all projects of the group) or project (only the projects of the file).

options.name: testsCountAsUse
options.description: Uses in test projects count; when off, a member used only by tests is reported as such.

options.name: stringLiteralsCountAsUse
options.description: The name as a string literal ('Name') counts as a use (RTTI, MethodAddress, scripts).

options.name: keepAttributes
options.description: Attributes on the member or its type that mark it as used, e.g. "Keep" or "Api".

options.name: keepPatterns
options.description: Name patterns (* and ?) for members that are always considered used, e.g. "TPlugin.*" or "*Callback".

rules.name: Declaration in the implementation section never used
rules.description: A routine, type, constant or global variable declared in the implementation section of a unit (or in a program or library) is used nowhere in the unit; the compiler does not report these. Any occurrence of the name as an identifier counts as a use, also in inactive conditional branches; not counted are the declarations themselves (including forward declarations), occurrences in the routine's own body (recursion) and, for types, occurrences in their own declaration and in the bodies of their own methods including the TType.Name header. For attribute classes (XyzAttribute) the short form [Xyz] counts. Considered used (service shared with unused-public-member): exported routines, declarations with attributes, names matching deadCode.keepPatterns, types with an attribute from deadCode.keepAttributes, and names from the form file. Bodies of interface routines are left to unused-public-member. Silent for units with include files. Quick fix: mark as intentionally present (lsp-ignore comment).
rules.bad:
implementation

procedure AltesFormat(const AText: string);  // called nowhere
begin
end;

rules.name: Unit not used by any other unit
rules.description: A unit of an application is used by no other unit of the uses graph: at most programs name it in their uses clause, and they use none of its identifiers outside the uses clause (Application.CreateForm(TForm1, Form1) counts as a use). Units with an initialization or finalization section (registrations, side effects at start-up) count as used. Medium confidence: code outside the project group, scripts or packages loaded at run time can still use the unit. Silent for units of packages and libraries (users outside the group) unless projectKinds allows them, without projects, while projects are loading or the index is incomplete, and for units the uses graph does not know. Reported at the unit name in the header.
rules.bad:
program App;
uses
  Haupt,
  AltExport;  // AltExport is used nowhere else

options.name: projectKinds
options.description: Project kinds whose units are checked: application, package, library.

rules.name: Message method declared incorrectly
rules.description: A message procedure of a class does not have exactly one var parameter (like E2138; the parameter type is not checked, an untyped var parameter is fine), its message number is less than 1 (like E2139), or an earlier message method of the same class already handles the same number (like E2140, usually after copying). Numbers count as equal when their values are known (numbers, constants from the index) or when the expressions are the same text. Methods in mutually exclusive {$IF} branches are not duplicates; the same number in a descendant overrides the handler and is fine. Quick fix for E2138: make a single parameter var, otherwise replace the list with (var Msg: TMessage); the method body in the same file is adjusted as well.
rules.bad:
procedure WMSize(var Msg: TWMSize); message WM_SIZE;
procedure WMGroesse(var Msg: TWMSize); message WM_SIZE;
rules.good:
procedure WMSize(var Msg: TWMSize); message WM_SIZE;
procedure WMMove(var Msg: TWMMove); message WM_MOVE;

rules.name: Invalid declaration in an interface
rules.description: An interface type declares something interfaces cannot have: fields (like E2209), visibility sections or method directives such as virtual, dynamic, abstract, override, message or reintroduce (like E2210), the property clauses stored, nodefault or default with a value (like E2207; default; after an array property is fine), or a property an ancestor interface already declares, listed again without a type (like E2206; a redeclaration with a type compiles, also with inherited accessors). A class, record or enumeration as the ancestor of an interface or in the interface list of a class is reported as well (like E2205), and so is the same interface twice in that list (like E2208). Types are resolved through the uses clauses; aliases, unknown types, dispinterfaces and declarations inside conditional branches stay silent.

rules.name: Invalid implements clause
rules.description: Delegation with implements breaks one of its fixed rules: implements only in classes (like E2258), only on properties of class or interface type (like E2259; reported for built-in types, records and enumerations), not together with index (like E2260), only on readable properties (like E2261), the getter without a calling convention other than register (like E2262) and not dynamic or message (like E2263), each interface implemented by one property only (like E2257) and no method resolution clause for an interface implemented that way (like E2264). Types are resolved through the uses clauses; unknown types, aliases and properties in conditional branches stay silent.
rules.bad: property Logger: ILogger write FLogger implements ILogger;
rules.good: property Logger: ILogger read FLogger write FLogger implements ILogger;

rules.name: Calling convention does not fit
rules.description: The compiler prescribes the calling convention here: constructors and destructors of a class only with register (like E2236), getters and setters of published properties as well (like E2270), and varargs only with cdecl (like E2277 for external routines, otherwise E2591). Explicit register is fine; class constructors, accessors outside published sections and inherited accessors stay silent. Quick fix: remove the convention in the declaration and in the method body of the same file, or set cdecl for varargs.
rules.bad: function Formatieren(Muster: PAnsiChar): Integer; stdcall; varargs; external 'msvcrt.dll';
rules.good: function Formatieren(Muster: PAnsiChar): Integer; cdecl; varargs; external 'msvcrt.dll';

rules.name: Invalid dispinterface declaration
rules.description: A dispinterface breaks one of its fixed rules: no ancestor in parentheses (like E2228), a GUID is required (like E2229), methods take no directives except dispid and the hints deprecated, platform, library and experimental (like E2230; reported are calling conventions and binding directives such as virtual, overload stays silent) and properties take no read or write (like E2231; use readonly, writeonly or dispid). Forward declarations and declarations in conditional branches stay silent. Quick fixes: remove the ancestor, insert a GUID, remove the directive.
rules.bad: DAnzeige = dispinterface(IBasis) ['{6A0F0D5E-1C11-4B8E-9A43-3F1D4C2A2228}'] procedure Machen; stdcall; dispid 1; end;
rules.good: DAnzeige = dispinterface ['{6A0F0D5E-1C11-4B8E-9A43-3F1D4C2A2228}'] procedure Machen; dispid 1; end;

rules.name: abstract, final or static combined wrongly
rules.description: A method directive the compiler rejects: abstract without virtual, dynamic or override (like E2167), a body in the implementation section for an abstract method (like E2136), final on a method that is not virtual (like E2351), abstract together with final (like E2371), a class declared abstract sealed (like E2383, E2540) or static on an instance method or a virtual class method (like E2376). A body only counts for an abstract method when no non-abstract method of the same name in the same class is compiled with it (overloads, {$IFDEF} branches). Quick fixes: insert virtual; before abstract, remove the body.

rules.name: Forward declaration never satisfied
rules.description: A routine declared in the interface section or with forward has no body (like E2065), or a forward declaration TFoo = class; or IFoo = interface; is never completed in the same type section (like E2086, E2420). Methods are checked by declared-not-implemented. A body fits when it has the same name; with overload the number of parameters must match too. An external declaration in the implementation section counts as a body. Declarations inside a {$IFDEF} branch are skipped; with include files the rule does not check routines. Quick fix: create an empty body before initialization or the final end.
rules.bad:
interface

function Pruefsumme(const Daten: TBytes): Cardinal;

implementation

end.

rules.name: Member hides a member of the ancestor
rules.description: A property has the name of a field of an ancestor (like W1009), a field has the name of a field or property of an ancestor, or a non-virtual method has the name and parameters of a non-virtual method of an ancestor. Code that accesses the object through the ancestor type still sees the old member. Virtual methods are reported by hides-virtual, local names by shadowed-name. Republished properties (property Caption;), properties with a new type over an ancestor property, overload, reintroduce, constructors and class methods are not reported. Members the descendant cannot see (private in another unit, strict private with ignoreStrictPrivate) are skipped; ancestors come from the file and the symbol index. Quick fix for fields and properties: rename the member in the class declaration and the bodies of its methods in this unit (FName becomes FKundeName).

options.name: ignoreStrictPrivate
options.description: Do not report hidden strict private members of the ancestor.

rules.name: Invalid member in the published section
rules.description: A member behind an explicit published that the compiler rejects: a property of a static array, pointer or plain procedural type (like E2188; records and dynamic arrays compile), of type Real48 (like E2186) or of a set larger than 4 bytes (like E2187), a field that is neither a class nor an interface (like E2217), more than one published overload (like E2266), a class property (like E2545) or a name with non-ASCII characters (like E2452). Types are resolved through the file and the index, aliases are followed; type parameters, unknown types and sections whose published is in another conditional branch than the member stay silent. The section without visibility specifier is not checked, because the compiler silently demotes such members to public there. Quick fix: move the member into the public section.

rules.name: Spelling or visibility differs from the ancestor
rules.description: An overriding method spells its name differently from the ancestor (destructor destroy, like H2365) or has a lower visibility than the overridden method (like H2269, only for classes in the interface section; visibilities are compared in tiers private, protected, public), a getter or setter is named Get<Property> or Set<Property> but spelled differently (like H2367), or an inline method accesses a member that is less visible than the method itself, so the compiler cannot expand it outside the class (like H2440). Matters for C++Builder users of the units and for consistent code. The docwiki lists H2269 and H2367 as X2269 and X2367 because their level can be changed; dcc reports them as hints by default. H2368 and H2369 are not covered, since it is not documented when dcc reports them. Off by default; switch it on in atlas.json. Quick fixes: adopt the ancestor's spelling, rename the accessor.

rules.name: default property declared wrongly or missing
rules.description: default; behind a property without index parameters (like E2132), a second default property of the same class with the same index types (like E2131; overloading by index type is allowed), or Obj[I] on a class that has no default property in its whole ancestor chain (like E2149). The type of Obj is resolved by name resolution; unresolvable types, broken ancestor chains and classes with a class helper in the unit stay silent. Property redeclarations without a type (property Items; default;) take the index from the ancestor and are not checked.

rules.name: Redeclared property missing in the ancestor
rules.description: A property redeclaration without type such as property Caption; (to change the visibility or the default value) names a property that no ancestor has (like E2147), or the ancestor's property is not accessible from here: strict private, or private in another unit (like E2233). Only reported when the whole ancestor chain is known; a field or method of the same name and declarations in inactive conditional branches stay silent. Quick fix: use the most similar property name of the ancestors.

rules.name: Inline function is not expanded
rules.description: A call of an inline routine from another unit that the compiler does not expand: its body needs a unit that is missing from uses here (like H2443, typically System.Generics.Collections for TJSONObject.Count), it accesses a strict private member and the call is not inside a method of that class (like H2444), the calling routine is inline itself and the unit of the callee is only in the implementation uses (like H2445), or the unit of the callee uses this unit directly (like H2456) or through other units (like H2457). Calls, properties with an inline getter or setter and for-in loops (GetEnumerator, MoveNext, Current) are checked. The index records what each inline body refers to; the rule only reports what it resolves for sure (unknown references and members inherited from other units stay silent). Silent with {$INLINE OFF} in the file. Quick fix: add the missing units to the uses clause of the section.
rules.bad:
uses
  System.JSON;
...
for Wert in Feld as TJSONArray do
rules.good:
uses
  System.JSON, System.Generics.Collections;
...
for Wert in Feld as TJSONArray do

rules.name: Unknown directive (typo)
rules.description: A word that is not a directive stands where a directive belongs: after the ';' of a routine or method header (overide;, virutal;, overlaod;, stdcal;, reintroduces;) or after a property, where only default is allowed (defualt;). The compiler stops there (like E2070). The message suggests the closest directive when at most two characters differ. Silent in {$IF} branches that test FPC, which knows further directives such as nostackframe. Quick fix: replace with the suggested directive.
rules.bad: procedure Paint; overide;
rules.good: procedure Paint; override;

rules.name: Dialog in a console program or service
rules.description: ShowMessage, ShowMessageFmt, MessageDlg, TaskMessageDlg, InputBox, InputQuery, Application.MessageBox or TDialogService in a program with {$APPTYPE CONSOLE} (or DCC_ConsoleTarget in the .dproj), in a Windows service or in a DLL without forms. In a service the dialog blocks invisibly; a console program waits for a click nobody sees when it runs unattended. A service is a unit with a class derived from TService, or any unit of a project whose .dpr uses Vcl.SvcMgr without Vcl.Forms. A DLL without forms is a library whose .dpr lists no form and does not use Vcl.Forms; there the rule reports with medium confidence, because only the host decides whether there is a user interface. Units with a form file, calls under if IsConsole and routines of the same name declared in the unit stay silent. Counterpart of writeln-in-gui-app. High confidence. No quick fix: log the message instead of showing it.

rules.name: Loading or saving text without an encoding
rules.description: LoadFromFile, SaveToFile, LoadFromStream or SaveToStream of a TStrings (TStringList, Memo.Lines, ListBox.Items, Query.SQL) and TFile.ReadAllText or TFile.ReadAllLines without an encoding: a file without BOM is read with the ANSI code page of the machine, and SaveToFile writes ANSI, so umlauts get lost between machines. The receiver must be a declared string list or a Lines, Items, SQL or Strings property; bitmaps, streams and datasets stay silent. Also silent when the list sets DefaultEncoding anywhere in the unit or was loaded with an encoding earlier in the same routine (SaveToFile then keeps that encoding). TFile.WriteAllText, TStreamReader and TStreamWriter already default to UTF-8 and are not reported. Medium confidence. Quick fix: add TEncoding.UTF8 (option defaultEncoding) as the last argument and System.SysUtils to uses.
rules.bad: Zeilen.LoadFromFile(Pfad);
rules.good: Zeilen.LoadFromFile(Pfad, TEncoding.UTF8);

options.name: defaultEncoding
options.description: TEncoding property the quick fix inserts: UTF8, Unicode, BigEndianUnicode, ANSI, ASCII, UTF7 or Default.

rules.name: Writing to HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE
rules.description: RootKey := HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE on a TRegistry followed in the same routine by a writing access on the same object: OpenKey(…, True), CreateKey, Write…, DeleteKey, DeleteValue, RenameValue, MoveKey, SaveKey or RestoreKey. Without administrator rights this fails or silently lands in the registry virtualization. Use HKEY_CURRENT_USER for user settings; exclude installer code through exclude. Reading (OpenKeyReadOnly, Read…, OpenKey(…, False)), another RootKey before the write and writes in the other branch of {$IFDEF} stay silent. High confidence. Quick fix: RootKey := HKEY_CURRENT_USER.

rules.name: Elapsed time measured with Now
rules.description: A variable set to Now and later used in Now - Start, End - Start or MilliSecondsBetween, SecondsBetween, MinutesBetween, HoursBetween, DaysBetween or the …Span functions in the same routine: it measures elapsed time with the wall clock, which is coarse and wrong across daylight saving changes or clock synchronisation. TStopwatch is precise and monotonic. Assignments in another routine (fields) and in the other branch of {$IFDEF} stay silent. High confidence. Quick fix when the variable is a local TDateTime (also var Start := Now) used only for MilliSecondsBetween, SecondsBetween or MinutesBetween with Now: TStopwatch.StartNew and ElapsedMilliseconds (div 1000 or div 60000), the variable becomes Uhr when the name is free, System.Diagnostics is added to uses.

rules.name: Money amount as floating point
rules.description: Field, variable, parameter or property whose name denotes a money amount (option namePatterns) with type Double, Single, Extended or Real: binary floating point rounds cent amounts wrongly (0.1 + 0.2), Currency calculates them exactly. The last part of the name counts (GesamtPreis, Nettobetrag, FNetto, Preise; not NettoGewicht); rates, factors, quotas, shares (Steuersatz, PriceFactor) and checksums stay silent. Ambiguous words (Amount, Summe, Sum, Total: a quantity or sum of anything) only count with a money context in the type or routine: another money name, Currency or words like Cent, Euro, Rabatt, Invoice, Payment, Kosten (Lighten(AColor, AAmount: Double) stays silent). Off by default and low confidence: it shows up once the rule is switched on and minConfidence is low. Quick fix when all names of the declaration are money amounts: type Currency, for parameters also in the header of the implementation, for fields and properties also the property or the field behind read and write; no fix when a getter or setter would have to change too. With checkRound the rule also reports Round with a money amount in the argument (banker's rounding: 2.5 becomes 2).

options.name: namePatterns
options.description: Name parts that denote a money amount; plurals included.

options.name: checkRound
options.description: Also report Round on money amounts.

rules.name: Long if chain over the same string
rules.description: An if … else if chain that compares the same string (identifier or A.B, no function calls) with at least min literals: S = 'x', 'x' = S, SameText(S, 'x'), also combined with or, in at least two branches (a single if with or stays silent). case IndexStr(S, [...]) of or a dictionary is shorter and faster. Only comparisons that are always compiled together with the head count ({$IFDEF} branches inside the chain do not). Off by default, high confidence. Quick fix as in the code action if chain to case (#646): case IndexStr(…) of, IndexText(…) for SameText, comparisons joined with or share one label, the rest of the chain becomes else, System.StrUtils is added to uses. No fix when comments or directives sit between the branches, a literal appears twice or = and SameText are mixed.
rules.bad:
if Befehl = 'neu' then Neu
else if Befehl = 'oeffnen' then Oeffnen
else if Befehl = 'speichern' then Speichern
else if Befehl = 'beenden' then Beenden;

options.name: min
options.description: Number of comparisons of the same string from which the rule reports; at least 2.

rules.name: if chain can be written as case
rules.description: An if … else if chain with at least min branches (the final else counts) that compares the same ordinal expression (integer, character, enumeration; no side effects, no function call) with constants: X = a, a = X, X in [a, b..c], (X >= a) and (X <= b), also combined with or. Labels must be literals, constant expressions, untyped constants or enumeration values, without duplicates or overlaps. The type comes from name resolution; chains with unknown types and chains with directives stay silent. Off by default, high confidence. Quick fix: the code action In case umwandeln (#646, refactoring.ifCase); begin … end only where a branch has several statements, comments in the branches stay.
rules.bad:
if Kind = 1 then Neu
else if (Kind = 2) or (Kind = 3) then Oeffnen
else if (Kind >= 4) and (Kind <= 6) then Speichern
else Beenden;

options.name: min
options.description: Number of branches (the final else included) from which the rule reports; at least 2.

rules.name: Condition is always the same
rules.description: The condition of if, while or until is fixed: True, False, comparisons of numbers and untyped constants of the file, also through and, or, xor and not (X or True is always true, X and False always false). The branch is dead code or always runs. while True do and repeat … until False count as deliberate endless loops (infinite-loop checks their exit). Constants listed in switchConstants, constants inside a {$IF…} branch and constants from other units count as unknown. Quick fix for if: remove the dead branch or the condition.
rules.bad:
if (Count > 0) or True then
  Process;
rules.good:
if Count > 0 then
  Process;

options.name: switchConstants
options.description: Constants that deliberately serve as switches; conditions on them are not reported.

rules.name: Loop without exit
rules.description: while True do, repeat … until False or another loop whose condition never ends it, without an exit in the body: no Break (a Break in a nested loop only leaves that loop), Exit, raise, goto, Halt, Abort or RunError, no call of a routine of the file that raises an exception or ends the program, and no check of Terminated (thread loops are covered by thread-loop-without-terminated). Anonymous methods in the body do not count. The action jumps to the loop head.

rules.name: Loop condition never changes in the body
rules.description: No variable of the while or until condition changes in the body: no assignment, no Inc/Dec, no argument (possibly var), no method or member access on the object of the condition, no for loop over it. Typically a forgotten Inc(I) or Next. The rule only reports when every variable of the condition is a local variable or value parameter of the routine and at least one appears directly (not only as X.Property). Conditions with function calls, fields, global variables, var and out parameters and Terminated are not reported, nor loops with an exit (Break, Exit, raise …), waiting loops (Sleep, ProcessMessages …), with, calls of local routines or variables captured by an anonymous method. Changes through X[…] count only when the condition reads X[…].

rules.name: Loop runs at most once
rules.description: Every path through the body of a for, for-in, while or repeat loop ends with Exit, Break, raise, Halt, Abort, RunError, ExitProcess or a call of a routine of the file that raises, so the loop runs at most once. Usually an if is missing before the jump, or Continue was meant. A path counts as a jump for if with else and both branches, case with else and all branches, try … finally with the try or the finally part and try … except with the try part and every handler. Silent with Continue of this loop, goto or labels and conditional directives in the body; Break of inner loops does not count. Complements infinite-loop and loop-condition-unchanged. No quick fix, the intent is unclear; if the jump directly follows an if without else, the message asks whether it belongs into the if branch. High confidence.

options.name: allowFirstElement
options.description: Do not report a for-in loop of simple statements that ends with Exit or Break (fetching the first element).

rules.name: Recursion without a stop
rules.description: A routine calls itself on every path before it can return: there is no path without a self-call and no Exit or raise before it. The result is a stack overflow. Paths without a call are: an if without else or a case without else, the body of while and for, the right side of and/or, branches of if expressions and anonymous methods. Getters and setters of their own property are reported by setter-recursion; overloaded routines stay silent (the call may go to another overload). The margin marker from #623 shows every recursion.

rules.name: Arguments of Pos swapped
rules.description: Pos(Text, ';'): Pos, PosEx, AnsiPos, StartsText, StartsStr, EndsText and EndsStr (also with Ansi prefix) expect the searched part first and the text second; ContainsText and ContainsStr expect the text first. Reported when a short literal (up to maxLiteralLength characters, default 3; '' counts as one character, #9 as well) stands where the text belongs and a certain string stands where the part belongs: a variable or field of a string type declared in the file, .Text or .Caption, a string function of the RTL (Trim, UpperCase, Copy-like LeftStr, Format …) or a concatenation with a string part. Characters stay silent, because Pos(C, ';,') deliberately checks whether C is one of the separators; so do unknown types, two literals and methods of other objects (Liste.Pos). Medium confidence. Quick fix: swap the arguments in one edit; comments between them stay.
rules.bad: if Pos(Zeile, ';') > 0 then
rules.good: if Pos(';', Zeile) > 0 then

options.name: maxLiteralLength
options.description: Longest literal in the place of the text that is still taken as swapped.

rules.name: Integer division assigned to a floating-point number
rules.description: Average := Sum div Count with Average: Double: div cuts off the fraction before the value is assigned. Also Percent := Part div Total * 100, Result of a function with a floating-point result and var X: Double := A div B. The div is searched through parentheses, signs and + - * /, not inside calls (Round(A div B)), indexes, mod or comparisons. The target must be a variable, field (also Self.X) or Result whose type Single, Double, Extended, Real, Currency … is declared in the file. TDateTime, TDate and TTime stay silent (whole days are usually intended there), as do assignments inside with and Trunc(A) div Trunc(B) (also Round, Floor, Ceil: explicitly converted, so integer division is intended). High confidence. Quick fix: replace div with / (same precedence).

rules.name: Empty finally block
rules.description: A finally block without statements: usually the release got lost during a rework. If the statement right before try is X := T….Create, the message names X.Free. A block with an explaining comment counts as deliberate and is not reported (as with empty-except); a block with a compiler directive is skipped as well, because another branch may contain code. High confidence. Quick fix: remove try, finally and end and outdent the body (when try, finally and end each stand on their own line); as the only statement of an if, while, for, with or case branch with several statements in the body, try becomes begin.

rules.name: Form unit without {$R *.dfm}
rules.description: A .dfm or .fmx lies next to the unit and the unit declares the class of its root object, but no {$R …} directive includes a form file: creating the form raises EResNotFound. Conversely, a {$R *.dfm} or {$R Name.dfm} whose file does not exist next to the unit is reported (the compiler stops with F1026). A directive in any branch of conditional compilation counts as included. Silent when the form file's class is not declared in the unit and when the rule cannot see files next to the unit. Quick fix: insert {$R *.dfm} (or {$R *.fmx}) after implementation.
rules.bad:
implementation

procedure TfrmKunde.FormShow(Sender: TObject);

rules.name: Form created automatically and by hand
rules.description: The .dpr creates a form with Application.CreateForm, and the code also assigns TfrmX.Create(…) to the same global variable. There are then two instances; the first one stays invisible in memory. The automatically created forms come from the .dpr of the project the unit belongs to; when the rule can read the .dpr, the class must match the CreateForm call. Silent when the routine checks the variable (Assigned, comparison with nil) or frees it before (Free, FreeAndNil, Release), for local names and for fields of the own class with the same name, and for units without a project. High confidence. Quick fix: remove the Application.CreateForm line from the .dpr (the form is then only created by the code).

rules.name: Event handler in an inherited form without inherited
rules.description: With form inheritance, an ancestor form assigns a handler of the same name to the same event of the same component, but the handler in the descendant does not call inherited (any more). The IDE generates inherited; when the handler is created; once it is deleted, the logic of the ancestor is lost silently. The ancestor's form file comes from the index (file of the class) or from the units in the uses clause next to the unit; the chain follows inherited forms up to the first form with object. Handlers with a different name count as a deliberate replacement. Silent without the ancestor's form file. High confidence. Quick fix: insert inherited; at the start.

rules.name: Form frees itself in its own event
rules.description: Free, Destroy, DisposeOf or FreeAndNil on Self, or on the global variable of the form's own class, as a statement in an event handler of the form or one of its controls. After the handler returns, the VCL still accesses the object: access violation. Correct is Release, or Action := caFree in OnClose. Event handlers are the methods named in the form file and methods with a Sender: TObject parameter; a form is the root class of the form file with ClientWidth or ClientHeight, or a class derived directly from TForm or TCustomForm (frames and data modules have no Release). Statements in anonymous methods and with blocks do not count. Silent without the form file. High confidence. Quick fix: replace Free with Release; in OnClose (var Action: TCloseAction) with Action := caFree.

rules.name: Shared variable written in TParallel.For
rules.description: The body of TParallel.For, or of a TTask.Run/Create/Future started inside a loop, writes a variable from outside without a lock: Summe := Summe + …, Inc/Dec or another assignment, or changes a collection from outside (Add, Delete, Clear, Insert, Remove …). The iterations run at the same time, so additions get lost or the list is corrupted. Outside means a local variable or parameter of the enclosing routine, a field of its class or a global variable of the unit; names of unknown origin stay silent. Bodies with a lock (TMonitor, Enter, Acquire, Lock, LockList, BeginWrite, TInterlocked), writes through an index (Werte[I] := …) and nested anonymous methods (Synchronize, Queue) do not count. Types listed in threadSafeTypes count as thread-safe. Medium confidence. Quick fixes: TInterlocked.Add/Increment/Decrement for Integer, Int64 and Cardinal (adds System.SyncObjs), System.TMonitor.Enter/Exit in try … finally around the collection call.

options.name: threadSafeTypes
options.description: Types that count as thread-safe; their collection calls stay silent.

rules.name: Counter in a thread without TInterlocked
rules.description: Inc, Dec, X := X + 1 or X := X - 1 without a lock on a global variable in Execute of a TThread descendant, or on a field or global variable in the body of TTask.Run/Create/Future outside loops and of TThread.CreateAnonymousThread. Inc is not atomic: when several threads count at the same time, increments get lost. Thread classes come from the unit (also through intermediate classes) and from the index. Own fields of the thread in Execute and captured local variables of a single task have only one writer and stay silent, as do bodies with a lock (TMonitor, Enter, Acquire, Lock, LockList, BeginWrite, TInterlocked) and nested anonymous methods (Synchronize, Queue). Tasks inside loops and TParallel.For are reported by parallel-for-shared-write. Medium confidence. Quick fix: TInterlocked.Increment/Decrement/Add for Integer, Int64 and Cardinal (adds System.SyncObjs).

rules.name: Error in a constant expression
rules.description: A constant expression divides by zero (like E2098), overflows beyond the range of Int64 and UInt64 (like E2099), a range has its low bound above its high bound (array[5..1], like E2011), a constant violates an integer type of fixed size or a subrange type (like W1012, reported as a warning; assignments only from values outside 0..127) or a hex, binary or octal literal needs more than 64 bits (like E2102). Atlas evaluates literals, constants (also from other units) and SizeOf/High/Low of types with a fixed size; a constant from an {$IF} branch only counts where the checked place is compiled together with it. Expressions with unknown parts stay silent.

rules.name: Invalid default value of a parameter
rules.description: Default values the compiler rejects: several names sharing one default value (A, B: Integer = 0, like E2237), a parameter without a default value after one with a default value (like E2238), var and out parameters with a default value (like E2239) records or static arrays with a default value (like E2268) and sets larger than 4 bytes with a default value (like E2146, only small sets are allowed; medium confidence). Applies to routines, methods and procedural types. Quick fixes: declare the parameters one by one; move the parameters with a default value to the end, also in the matching declaration or implementation header of the same file (calls are not changed).
rules.bad: procedure Senden(const Text: string = ''; Ziel: TZiel);
rules.good: procedure Senden(Ziel: TZiel; const Text: string = '');

rules.name: Signed and unsigned mixed
rules.description: Comparison or arithmetic (+, -, *, div, mod) with one signed and one unsigned operand whose types are known for certain (variables, fields, properties, function results, own aliases). With UInt64 the whole expression is computed unsigned and a negative value becomes a huge number (like W1073, comparison like W1023); with Cardinal/DWORD and a signed type up to 32 bits both operands are widened to Int64 (like W1023/W1024). Silent for Byte and Word, Cardinal with Int64, literals, constants, NativeInt/NativeUInt and unknown types. Medium confidence. Quick fix: convert the unsigned operand to Int64.
rules.bad: if Groesse + Delta < Grenze then  // Groesse: UInt64; Delta: Int64
rules.good: if Int64(Groesse) + Delta < Grenze then

rules.name: Assignment with possible data loss
rules.description: An assignment or an inline variable with a value whose type is wider than the target, without an explicit conversion: Int64 to Integer, NativeInt to Integer (Win64) and, via the option types, e.g. Double to Single or Extended to Double. Like W1071 (integers), W1072 (floating point) and W1066 (Extended to Double); the compiler shows W1071 only when switched on. Only reported when both types are known for certain (variables, fields, properties, function results, own aliases and integer arithmetic built from them); literals and explicit conversions stay silent. Off by default; medium confidence. Quick fixes: convert explicitly; widen the type of the target's declaration (single variable declared in the same file).
rules.bad: Anzahl := Strom.Size;  // Anzahl: Integer
rules.good: Anzahl := Integer(Strom.Size);

options.name: types
options.description: Reported pairs source type>target type, e.g. Double>Single or Extended>Double.

rules.name: Typed constant modified
rules.description: A typed constant (const Counter: Integer = 0) is assigned (like W1017, also an element or a record field of it) or passed as a var or out argument, including Inc, Dec, Include, Exclude, Delete, SetLength and the like (like W1016). Usually a variable was meant; this only compiles with {$J+}, and with {$J+} in effect before the declaration the rule stays silent like dcc. When {$J-} or {$WRITEABLECONST OFF} is in effect before the declaration in the same file or in a file it includes before that point, it is reported as an error (like E2064 or E2197). Also reports 0 as the value of a pointer constant or an initialised pointer variable (like W1013). Quick fixes: turn a unit-level constant into a variable with an initial value (the const section is split if needed; local typed constants keep their value between calls and get no fix); write nil instead of 0.

rules.name: String limit exceeded
rules.description: A string literal is truncated to fit a string[N] or ShortString target: assignment, typed constant or initialised variable, also via own aliases, string[Constant] and fields from other units (like W1014). Before Delphi 12 (delphiVersion below 23) a quoted literal may have at most 255 characters (like E2056), and a resourcestring may have at most 4096 characters, literals joined with + included (like E2381); both are errors. Characters are counted as written, '' and #13 count as one. Quick fixes: declare the target as string (single variable or typed constant of the same file; record fields keep their size); split the literal into pieces of 255 characters joined with +.

rules.name: New, Dispose or SetLength misused on a dynamic array
rules.description: New (like E2255) or Dispose (like E2256) on a dynamic array, SetLength without a length (like E2246), New with a length on a type that is not a dynamic array (like E2307) and New(TArrayType) without a length (like E2308). Typical for old code that switched from pointers to dynamic arrays. The rule only reports when name resolution knows the variable or type for sure; aliases are followed (TValues = array of Double), TBytes and the other dynamic arrays of the RTL count even without an index; open array parameters and pointers stay silent. Quick fixes: Dispose(A) becomes A := nil, New(A) becomes SetLength(A, 1).
rules.bad: Dispose(Werte);
rules.good: Werte := nil;

rules.name: Local routine as procedure variable
rules.description: A local (nested) routine is assigned to a variable or passed to a parameter of a procedural type without of object (like E2094), or a typed constant of a routine takes the address of a local variable (like E2278). Usually an anonymous method or a routine of the unit was meant. The rule only reports when name resolution knows the target type for sure; method pointers and method references stay silent because the compiler reports them with other codes, and so does @Routine (an untyped pointer). Quick fix: move the routine in front of the enclosing routine as a routine of the unit, if it uses nothing from it (no local names further out, no class members without a prefix).

rules.name: Integer and HRESULT interchanged
rules.description: A class implements an interface method with an HRESULT result through a method with an Integer (or LongInt) result, or the other way round (like X1008). Both are 32 bits wide, so it goes unnoticed, but the meaning of the values (S_FALSE as success) is lost; important for COM and Open Tools API code. Methods are matched by name and parameter types, including resolution clauses such as function IFoo.Bar = Baz; interfaces and their ancestors come from the file or the index. If variants stand in conditional branches, the rule only reports when every variant differs. Quick fix: align the result type in declaration and implementation with the interface.

rules.name: Invalid argument for a var or out parameter
rules.description: A var or out parameter receives something that is not a variable: a string element for a character parameter (like E2354), a constant, a const parameter, a property or a function result (like E2197), a constant for an open array (like E2192) or an expression (like E2036). Reported only for routines without overloads whose header is known from the file or the index; built-in routines such as Inc or Move and untyped var parameters accept more and stay silent. Typed constants count as constants unless {$J+} is set. Quick fix: pass a local variable of the parameter type, and write it back for string elements and properties with write.

rules.name: Condition is not Boolean
rules.description: The condition of if, while, until or a conditional expression has a type that is surely not Boolean: a number, a pointer, a class, an interface, a string or a character (like E2012). Unlike C, Delphi needs a Boolean. Reported only when the type is certain; Boolean types such as LongBool, enumerations, aliases and unknown types stay silent. Quick fix: add <> 0 (alternative > 0), <> nil (alternative Assigned), <> '' or <> #0.
rules.bad:
if Liste.Count then
  Verarbeiten;
rules.good:
if Liste.Count > 0 then
  Verarbeiten;

rules.name: for-in over a type without enumerator
rules.description: A for-in loop runs over a type that cannot be enumerated: a number, pointer, character or Boolean, or a class, record or interface without a public GetEnumerator, also not inherited or from a helper (like E2430); or the enumerator returned by GetEnumerator lacks a public MoveNext or Current (like E2431). Strings, arrays and sets are fine. Reported only when the type and all its ancestors are known; generic types and unknown types stay silent. No quick fix; if the type has Count, the message suggests an indexed loop.
rules.bad: for F in Felder.Dataset do
rules.good: for F in Felder do

rules.name: Expression or declaration lacks the required kind of type
rules.description: An operation needs a certain kind of type that the operand surely does not have: an index on a number, Boolean, character or enumeration (like E2016); ^ on such a value, a class, a record or an interface (like E2017); a dot or with on such a value (like E2018); an object type whose ancestor is not an object type, TypeOf on a simple value and Dispose with destructor on a pointer to a simple type (like E2019); a class whose ancestor is a record, class reference, enumeration or simple type (like E2021); a class helper whose ancestor is not a helper (like E2022); New with constructor on a pointer to a simple type (like E2467); a record helper for a class or interface (like E2474); a method without class called through the class type outside methods of that class and its descendants (like E2076); Slice outside an open array argument (like E2193); a record inside an array passed to array of const (like E2150); Write/Writeln or Read/Readln with a class, record or interface (like E2054, E2055). Reported only when the type is certain: unknown types, conditional declarations, visible helpers, units missing from the index, records with an Implicit operator and unknown ancestors stay silent. Quick fixes: remove ^ before a dot for classes, records and interfaces; write Object.ToString in Write/Writeln.
rules.bad:
Kunde^.Name := 'A';
Writeln(ErrOutput, Kunde);
rules.good:
Kunde.Name := 'A';
Writeln(ErrOutput, Kunde.ToString);

rules.name: inherited calls an abstract method
rules.description: inherited with an explicit method name, such as inherited Zeichnen(C), although the method is abstract in the ancestor (like E2373). A bare inherited; is skipped silently by the compiler for abstract methods and is not reported. The method is resolved by name resolution including overloads; the rule only reports when every matching overload is abstract. Quick fix: remove the call when it is a statement of its own in a begin…end block.

rules.name: Override only calls inherited
rules.description: An overriding method whose body only calls the inherited method: a bare inherited;, inherited Name or inherited Name(A, B) with its own parameters in unchanged order, in functions only Result := inherited Name(…). It does nothing of its own and pretends a changed behaviour. Silent when the method changes the visibility of the ancestor's method (protected to public), carries an attribute, default values or the directives final, deprecated, experimental, platform, library or reintroduce, has local declarations, more than one statement, comments or conditional directives in the body, or when the overridden method is unknown (ancestor not indexed; virtual methods of TObject count as public). High confidence. Quick fix: remove declaration and body, including XMLDoc comments and the blank line after the body.

rules.name: inherited without a method in the ancestor
rules.description: A bare inherited; in a method that no ancestor declares (a new method, no override) does nothing. This points to a forgotten override or a misspelled name. Not reported: message handlers (inherited calls DefaultHandler there), class and static methods, constructors and destructors, override and reintroduce, inherited inside anonymous methods, ancestors with a member of that name (also non-virtual) and unknown ancestors. Ancestors from other units come from the symbol index; methods of TObject count as known when System is not indexed. High confidence. Quick fix: remove inherited when it is a statement of its own in a begin…end block.

rules.name: Redundant Exit or Continue
rules.description: A bare Exit; as the last statement of a routine or anonymous method, or a bare Continue; as the last statement of a loop body (for, for-in, while, repeat), also in the last branch of an if at the end (the then branch only without else; then Continue else … guards an else-if chain). The jump changes nothing. Not reported: Exit with a value, jumps inside try…finally or try…except (the jump deliberately triggers the finally part), inside case, qualified names such as System.Continue, statements with a goto label and bodies with conditional directives. High confidence. Quick fix: remove the statement when it stands in a begin…end block or directly in repeat.

rules.name: Type argument violates a constraint
rules.description: A type argument does not satisfy the constraint of its type parameter: class (like E2511), record (like E2512), constructor (like E2513), an interface (like E2514) or a base class (like E2515). Inside methods of a generic type of this file the rule also reports T.Create without a constructor constraint (like E2568) and method calls on values of a type parameter without any constraint (like E2571). The generic type is resolved by name resolution including the number of type parameters, its constraints come from its declaration in the file or in the symbol index. Arguments that are type parameters themselves, aliases and types whose ancestry cannot be resolved are not reported. Quick fix for a type parameter of this file that stands alone in its group: add the constraint (T: class, constructor or T: class).

rules.name: Type in a declaration not found
rules.description: A type name in a declaration (field, parameter, result, ancestor, interface list, variable, type argument) is not declared (like E2003, for the target of a pointer type like E2564) or is not a type (like E2005). Complements unresolved-identifier, which only checks statements. Same preconditions as unresolved-attribute: System in the symbol index, every unit from uses known, not inside {$IF…} blocks. Type parameters, names the file declares as a type anywhere (also nested) and names the index knows as a nested type (inherited inner types) are not reported. Quick fix: add the unit that declares the type (with the same number of type parameters) to uses.

rules.name: Constructor called through a class reference is not virtual
rules.description: Create called through a class reference (class of TBasis) whose constructor is not virtual. On Win32 and Win64 this compiles silently but always runs the constructor of TBasis: fields that descendants set up in their own constructors stay empty (like E2391). The receiver may be a variable, field, parameter or function result whose type is a class reference; the constructor is resolved by name resolution in the nearest class that declares it, including overloads by argument count. The rule stays silent when a matching overload is virtual, dynamic, override or abstract, when a declaration lies in another branch of conditional compilation, and when a type cannot be resolved. Quick fix when the constructor is declared in this file: virtual on it and override on the constructors with the same signature in descendants in this file.

rules.name: Break, Continue or Exit in a place where it is not allowed
rules.description: Break or Continue outside a loop (like E2097), or Break, Continue or Exit that leave a finally block (like E2126). Delphi only reports both when compiling; it happens often after moving a loop body into a method of its own. A loop that lies entirely inside the finally block may use Break and Continue. Routines and anonymous methods start afresh: a Break in an anonymous method does not belong to the loop around it. Only plain calls are reported (not TMonitor.Exit(FLock)), and not when the file declares a routine or variable of that name. Quick fix outside a finally block: replace Break with Exit.
rules.bad:
if Eintrag.Treffer then
  Break;
rules.good:
if Eintrag.Treffer then
  Exit;

rules.name: raise without an argument outside a handler
rules.description: raise; without an exception object is only allowed in an except block (like E2145); Delphi only reports it when compiling. It happens in a local procedure called from the handler, in a finally block or after moving code. Routines and anonymous methods start afresh. The rule stays silent in anonymous methods inside an except block and in routines where the parser reports an error. No quick fix: raise a new exception (raise EImport.Create(…)) or move the code into the handler. reraise-exception-object covers raise E; inside the handler.
rules.bad:
Protokoll.Fehler('Import abgebrochen');
raise;
rules.good:
Protokoll.Fehler('Import abgebrochen');
raise EImportAbgebrochen.Create('Import abgebrochen');

rules.name: Label used incorrectly
rules.description: A label is set twice (like E2073), declared and jumped to but never set (E2074), set or jumped to without being declared in the current routine (E2093; a goto to a label declared nowhere and never set is reported by the syntax rule as E2031), or goto jumps into or out of a try block, also between the try part and its except or finally part (E2127). Delphi only reports these when compiling. Labels belong to one routine or the program block; a local procedure cannot jump to a label of the routine around it. Duplicate labels in conditional branches that exclude each other stay silent, as do routines with an asm block, because labels inside asm are not in the syntax tree. No quick fix.

rules.name: Loop variable changed or not local
rules.description: The variable of a for loop is assigned in the body or changed with Inc/Dec (like E2081), passed as a var or out parameter to a routine of this file (like W1015), or is not a simple local variable: a field of the own class, a global variable of the unit or a local variable of the enclosing routine (like E1019). Delphi only reports these when compiling. Parameters, unknown names and loops inside with statements stay silent, as do anonymous methods in the body and routines with parser errors. Quick fixes: convert to a while loop (not when the body uses Continue), or use for var when the routine does not use the name otherwise.

rules.name: Loop variable read after the loop
rules.description: After a for loop that ends normally (without Break), the loop variable is undefined. The rule reports the first read of the variable on a path from the normal loop exit, before it is assigned again (like W1037). Only simple local variables of the routine are checked; for var loops, fields, globals, reads only inside the body, arguments of routines that might be out parameters, and routines whose control flow is incomplete stay silent. Quick fix: convert to a while loop, where the counter has a defined value afterwards.

rules.name: Wrong number of arguments
rules.description: A call passes more arguments than the routine has parameters (like E2034) or fewer than its parameters without default value (like E2035), also as a statement without parentheses. Checked only when the name resolves to exactly one routine: overloads, varargs, typecasts, variables of procedural type, System identifiers without source and declarations in conditional branches are left to the compiler (E2250). A function called with too many arguments is only reported when its result type is known and not procedural. Quick fix: Signature help opens the parameter hint inside the parentheses (adds () when missing).
rules.bad: Versenden(Kunde.Mail, 'Rechnung');
rules.good: Versenden(Kunde.Mail, 'Rechnung', Text);

rules.name: Method does not need Self
rules.description: A method of a class or record uses neither Self nor instance members (fields, properties, instance methods, inherited). It is not virtual, not an event of the form file, does not implement an interface and is not used as a method pointer. Experimental: only active when switched on in atlas.json; silent with refactoring.methodKind off. Quick fix: turn into a class method (class … static with refactoring.methodKindStatic); the code actions also offer calls via the class, a free routine and a record helper for the type of the first parameter, each with a preview of all changed calls.
